title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試錄序
成化紀元之二十二年丙午
秋八月天下當開科試士浙
江寔為首藩先是
欽差鎮守司設監太監張慶巡按
監察御史荆茂咸祗若
國家興學育才盛典殫厥心力
===
罔敢少怠監察御史賀霖朱
守恕黎鼎各以事涖兹土胥
勤勸相以故士氣丕振於昔
既而藩臬兩司重臣承檄部
臺惟謹遂白諸巡按御史禮
聘祥與訓導桑悅充考試官
學正鄭時佐教諭李昌隆程
punctuated:
浙江鄉試錄序

成化紀元之二十二年丙午，秋八月，天下當開科試士，浙江寔為首藩。先是，欽差鎮守司設監太監張慶、巡按監察御史荆茂，咸祗若國家興學育才盛典，殫厥心力，罔敢少怠。監察御史賀霖、朱守恕、黎鼎，各以事涖兹土，胥勤勸相，以故士氣丕振於昔。既而藩臬兩司重臣承檄部臺惟謹，遂白諸巡按御史，禮聘祥與訓導桑悅充考試官，學正鄭時佐、教諭李昌隆、程
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

In the eighth month, in autumn, of the twenty-second year of the Chenghua era, the bingwu year (1486), examinations for scholars were due to be held throughout the realm. Zhejiang was indeed foremost among the provinces. Previously, Zhang Qing, Grand Eunuch of the Directorate of Imperial Regalia, imperially commissioned to serve as resident overseer, and Jing Mao, Regional Inspector and Investigating Censor, had both reverently upheld the state's grand institutions for promoting learning and nurturing talent. They devoted all their energies to this work, never daring to slacken in the least. Investigating Censors He Lin, Zhu Shoushu, and Li Ding, each visiting this region on official business, likewise diligently encouraged and assisted the undertaking. Consequently, the scholars' morale rose greatly above its former level.

Thereafter, the senior officials of the Provincial Administration Commission and Provincial Surveillance Commission scrupulously carried out directives from the ministry and censorial authorities. They then reported to the Regional Inspector and respectfully invited Xiang and Assistant Instructor Sang Yue to serve as Examiners, and School Instructor Zheng Shizuo, Instructor Li Changlong, and Cheng…

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
鳳儀訓導陸坦王統張磬梁
統李卞中充同考試官提督
學政副使李士實躬閱郡縣
士拔其尤者覆覈於巡按御
史得千九百有奇比入院提
調則左布政使端宏右參政
張敷華監試則按察使戴珊
===
僉事劉懋而右布政使閻鐸
右參政夏寅副使閻佐吳文
元左右參議李昊陳潭黃璉
僉事張玉李鑑柯燉汪山王
輔孫弁鄒霶相與贊理於外
若受卷彌封謄錄諸執事亦
旣遴選屬吏以充日之辛巳
punctuated: 鳳儀、訓導陸坦、王統、張磬、梁統、李卞中充同考試官。提督學政副使李士實躬閱郡縣士，拔其尤者，覆覈於巡按御史，得千九百有奇。比入院，提調則左布政使端宏、右參政張敷華，監試則按察使戴珊、僉事劉懋，而右布政使閻鐸、右參政夏寅、副使閻佐、吳文元、左右參議李昊、陳潭、黃璉、僉事張玉、李鑑、柯燉、汪山、王輔、孫弁、鄒霶，相與贊理於外。若受卷、彌封、謄錄諸執事，亦旣遴選屬吏以充。日之辛巳，
translation_en: … Fengyi, and Assistant Instructors Lu Tan, Wang Tong, Zhang Qing, Liang Tong, and Li Bianzhong served as Associate Examiners. Li Shishi, Surveillance Vice Commissioner charged with supervising education, personally examined the students of the prefectures and counties and selected the most outstanding. Following further scrutiny by the Regional Inspector, more than nineteen hundred were approved. When they entered the examination compound, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Duan Hong and Right Administration Vice Commissioner Zhang Fuhua served as Proctors; Surveillance Commissioner Dai Shan and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Liu Mao supervised the examination. Meanwhile, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Yan Duo; Right Administration Vice Commissioner Xia Yin; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Yan Zuo and Wu Wenyuan; Left and Right Administration Assistant Commissioners Li Hao, Chen Tan, and Huang Lian; and Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Zhang Yu, Li Jian, Ke Dun, Wang Shan, Wang Fu, Sun Bian, and Zou Pang jointly assisted with arrangements outside the compound. Subordinate officials had also been carefully selected to fill the various posts responsible for receiving papers, sealing candidates’ identifying information, and transcribing answers. On the xinsi day …

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之甲申之丁亥合諸士子而
三試之言之成文在理道純
正而不雜者如
定制取九十人巡按御史專監
臨之寄試事顛末無小大悉
綱紀之以雍以肅惟公惟慎
無間然也有錄用告厥成祥
===
僭序之仰惟
聖天子在位懸科設彀以待天下
之士風化攸繫非尋常政務
可比倫者祥等猥以文字蚤
被甄錄區區芹曝之私恒懼
莫之能遂迺今叨從禮聘以
柄文衡誠欲自效以少逭尸
punctuated:
之甲申、之丁亥，合諸士子而三試之。言之成文，在理道純正而不雜者，如定制取九十人。巡按御史專監臨之寄，試事顛末，無小大悉綱紀之，以雍以肅，惟公惟慎，無間然也。有錄，用告厥成，祥僭序之。
仰惟聖天子在位，懸科設彀，以待天下之士，風化攸繫，非尋常政務可比倫者。祥等猥以文字蚤被甄錄，區區芹曝之私，恒懼莫之能遂。迺今叨從禮聘，以柄文衡，誠欲自效，以少逭尸
translation_en:
…on the jiashen and dinghai days, the candidates were assembled and examined in three sessions. Ninety men whose compositions expressed pure and unadulterated moral principles were selected, in accordance with the established regulations. The Regional Inspector bore sole responsibility for supervision. From beginning to end, he directed every aspect of the examination, great and small, maintaining harmony and solemnity, fairness and care, with nothing open to criticism. A record was compiled to report its successful completion, and I, Xiang, have presumed to write its preface.
I respectfully reflect that the sagely Son of Heaven, reigning over the realm, has established examinations and set the bow’s range to receive scholars from throughout the empire. The transformation of customs depends upon this undertaking; it cannot be compared with ordinary administrative business. We, Xiang and the others, undeserving though we are, were selected early on for our literary abilities. In our modest desire to offer something of service—as humble as an offering of cress or the warmth of the sun—we have constantly feared that we might never fulfill that wish. Now, honored with a formal invitation to preside over the assessment of compositions, we sincerely wish to render service and thereby escape, in some small measure, the reproach of occupying office idly…

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
素其或私以隳行怠以荒業
非惟失人抑先失己祥不忍
爲也顧智力思慮有所不逮
舉置升落未能悉當人心心
之憂危如臨深谷夫以數人
之寡數昕夕之近萃千餘人
之辭藝手披目閱銖稱而寸
===
度之欲其無一失斯亦難矣
而况有陸敬輿乃識韓退之
有歐陽永叔乃識蘇軾轍曾
子固兩浙東南鉅省俊乂如
林每科必有異材以充他日
大受如祥之愚豈能於言語
文字中測而知之雖然言者
punctuated: 素。其或私以隳行，怠以荒業，非惟失人，抑先失己，祥不忍爲也。顧智力思慮有所不逮，舉置升落未能悉當人心，心之憂危，如臨深谷。夫以數人之寡，數昕夕之近，萃千餘人之辭藝，手披目閱，銖稱而寸度之，欲其無一失，斯亦難矣。而况有陸敬輿乃識韓退之，有歐陽永叔乃識蘇軾、轍、曾子固。兩浙，東南鉅省，俊乂如林，每科必有異材，以充他日大受。如祥之愚，豈能於言語文字中測而知之？雖然，言者
translation_en: …to escape, in some small measure, the reproach of drawing a salary without performing my duties. If I were to let partiality undermine my conduct or negligence ruin my work, I would not merely fail others but first fail myself. I, Xiang, cannot bear to do this. Yet my understanding, abilities, and deliberation have their limits; my decisions to select or set aside, advance or reject, cannot entirely satisfy everyone. My heart is anxious and apprehensive, as though I stood above a deep ravine. With so few examiners and so few days, we gather the literary compositions of more than a thousand candidates, open them by hand and read them with our eyes, weighing them ounce by ounce and measuring them inch by inch. To seek to make not a single error is indeed difficult. Moreover, it took Lu Jingyu to recognize Han Tuizhi, and Ouyang Yongshu to recognize Su Shi, Su Zhe, and Zeng Zigu. Liangzhe is a great province of the southeast, where outstanding men are as numerous as trees in a forest. Every examination must yield exceptional talents capable of shouldering great responsibilities in the future. How could someone as dull as I, Xiang, fathom and recognize them through their words and writings? Nevertheless, speech is…

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
心之聲也言之精者文也言
有醇駁而人品之邪正繇是
以別蓋精神心術之微有不
可得而掩者理固然也自鄉
舉里選之法不行於天下上
之所恃以登賢者舍言語文
字其將奚從因文以稽其言
===
因言以策其心盡吾力焉臧
否下上之間當不相遠此主
司所用以自解者也若夫勸
勉規箴之詞聖賢成法具在
宜無出乎諸士子之所肄習
之所講授者矣第恐行不及
知言浮其實今日之病往往
punctuated:
心之聲也，言之精者文也。言有醇駁，而人品之邪正繇是以別，蓋精神心術之微，有不可得而掩者，理固然也。自鄉舉里選之法不行於天下，上之所恃以登賢者，舍言語文字，其將奚從？因文以稽其言，因言以策其心，盡吾力焉，臧否下上之間，當不相遠。此主司所用以自解者也。

若夫勸勉規箴之詞，聖賢成法具在，宜無出乎諸士子之所肄習、之所講授者矣。第恐行不及知，言浮其實，今日之病往往
translation_en:
…is the voice of the heart, and writing is the refined expression of words. Words may be pure or mixed, and through them one can distinguish whether a person’s character is upright or depraved. For there are subtleties of spirit and inward disposition that cannot be concealed: this is necessarily so. Since the system of recommending worthy men from local communities ceased to operate throughout the realm, what means could those above rely upon to advance the worthy, apart from spoken and written words? By examining their writing to scrutinize their words, and through their words to assess their hearts, we exert ourselves to the utmost. Our judgments of merit and fault, and our rankings of higher and lower, should then not fall far from the truth. This is how those presiding over the examination reassure themselves.

As for words of encouragement and admonition, the established teachings of the sages and worthies are fully available; there should be nothing to add beyond what the candidates have studied and received instruction in. My only fear is that their conduct falls short of their knowledge, and their words exceed their actual attainments. The failings of the present day often…

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
坐此祥不佞不敢肆為陳說
以重多言之咎願與諸士子
以平日所能知能言者身體
而力行之
江西饒州府儒學教授林祥
謹序
punctuated:
坐此。祥不佞，不敢肆為陳說，以重多言之咎。願與諸士子以平日所能知、能言者，身體而力行之。
江西饒州府儒學教授林祥謹序。
translation_en:
…arises from this. I, Xiang, untalented as I am, dare not expound at length and thereby compound the fault of excessive speech. I wish, together with all you candidates, to embody personally and earnestly put into practice what we ordinarily know and can articulate.
Preface respectfully written by Lin Xiang, Instructor in the Confucian School of Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi.

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
自天子以至於庶人壹是皆以脩身為本
莫春者春服既成冠者五六人童子六七
人浴乎沂風乎舞雩詠而歸夫子喟然
嘆曰吾與點也
仰不愧於天俯不怍於人
易
首出庶物萬國咸寧
===
夬決也剛決柔也健而說決而和揚于王
庭柔乘五剛也
乾知大始坤作成物乾以易知坤以簡能
易則易知簡則易從易知則有親易從
則有功有親則可久有功則可大可久
則賢人之德可大則賢人之業易簡而
天下之理得矣天下之理得而成位乎
其中矣
其於人也為加憂為心病為耳痛為血卦
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

自天子以至於庶人，壹是皆以脩身為本。

莫春者，春服既成，冠者五六人，童子六七人，浴乎沂，風乎舞雩，詠而歸。夫子喟然嘆曰：「吾與點也！」

仰不愧於天，俯不怍於人。

易

首出庶物，萬國咸寧。

夬，決也，剛決柔也。健而說，決而和。「揚于王庭」，柔乘五剛也。

乾知大始，坤作成物。乾以易知，坤以簡能。易則易知，簡則易從。易知則有親，易從則有功。有親則可久，有功則可大。可久則賢人之德，可大則賢人之業。易簡而天下之理得矣；天下之理得，而成位乎其中矣。

其於人也，為加憂，為心病，為耳痛，為血卦，
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

From the Son of Heaven down to the common people, all alike take cultivating the self as the foundation.

“In late spring, when the spring clothes are ready, I would go with five or six men who have received their caps and six or seven boys to bathe in the Yi River, enjoy the breeze at the rain-dance altar, and return singing.” The Master sighed deeply and said, “I am with Dian!”

Looking up, to feel no shame before Heaven; looking down, to feel no shame before other people.

Book of Changes (Yi)

He rises above all beings as their head, and the myriad states are all at peace.

Guai means resolution: the firm resolves to remove the yielding. There is strength with joy, resolution with harmony. “Proclaimed in the royal court”: the yielding rides upon five firm lines.

Qian presides over the great beginning; Kun acts to bring things to completion. Qian presides through ease; Kun accomplishes through simplicity. What is easy is easy to understand; what is simple is easy to follow. What is easy to understand wins affinity; what is easy to follow achieves results. With affinity, one can endure; with results, one can attain greatness. Endurance is the virtue of the worthy; greatness is the achievement of the worthy. Through ease and simplicity, the principles of all under Heaven are grasped. When those principles are grasped, one establishes one’s place within Heaven and Earth.

In relation to human beings, it signifies increased anxiety, illness of the heart, and pain in the ears; it is the trigram of blood …

爲薄蹄爲曳
書

惟事事乃其有備有備無患

冢宰掌邦治統百官均四海

平王之孫齊侯之子
===
之子于苗選徒囂囂建旟設旄搏獸于敖
駕彼四牡四牡奕奕赤芾金舄會同有
繹决拾旣佽弓矢旣調射夫旣同助我
舉柴四黃旣駕兩驂不猗不失其馳舍
矢如破蕭蕭馬鳴悠悠旆旌徒御不驚
大庖不盈之子于征有聞無聲允矣君
子展也大成
文王有聲遹駿有聲遹求厥寧遹觀厥成
文王烝哉
punctuated:

書

惟事事乃其有備，有備無患。

詩
平王之孫，齊侯之子。
之子于苗，選徒囂囂。建旟設旄，搏獸于敖。駕彼四牡，四牡奕奕。赤芾金舄，會同有繹。决拾旣佽，弓矢旣調。射夫旣同，助我舉柴。四黃旣駕，兩驂不猗。不失其馳，舍矢如破。蕭蕭馬鳴，悠悠旆旌。徒御不驚，大庖不盈。之子于征，有聞無聲。允矣君子，展也大成。
文王有聲，遹駿有聲。遹求厥寧，遹觀厥成。文王烝哉！
translation_en:
…it represents red. In relation to horses, it represents a fine back, an anxious temperament, a lowered head, thin hooves, and a dragging gait.

Book of Documents
Ministers serve as my thighs and arms, my ears and eyes.
In every undertaking, make preparations; with preparations, there will be no calamity.
August Heaven has entrusted the people of the Central States and their territories to the former kings.
The Grand Steward directs the government of the realm, commands the hundred officials, and brings equitable order to all within the Four Seas.

Book of Odes
Grandchild of King Ping, child of the Marquis of Qi.
That lord goes on the summer hunt; the chosen foot soldiers gather in a clamorous throng. They raise the falcon banners and set up yak-tail standards, hunting beasts at Ao. They harness those four stallions, four splendid stallions. Wearing red knee covers and gold-adorned shoes, the lords assemble in an unbroken succession. Thumb rings and arm guards are fitted; bows and arrows are ready. The archers have assembled to help us raise the piled game. Four dun horses are harnessed; the two outer horses do not swerve. Keeping to their course as they gallop, the archers release arrows that strike as if splitting their targets. The horses neigh; the banners stream afar. Foot soldiers and charioteers remain composed; the great kitchen is not filled to excess. That lord goes forth: his renown is heard, yet there is no clamor. Trustworthy indeed is the noble lord; truly great is his achievement.
King Wen had renown—great indeed was his renown. He sought that peace; he surveyed that accomplishment. How glorious was King Wen!

The Duke of Lu, together with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao, met the king’s heir apparent at Shouzhi. 〔Fifth year of Duke Xi.〕 The Duke met the king’s representative, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, and Kuan, heir apparent of Chen, to conclude a covenant at Tao. 〔Eighth year of Duke Xi.〕 The Duke met the Grand Minister, the Duke of Zhou, the Marquis of Qi, the heir of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao at Kuiqiu. 〔Ninth year of Duke Xi.〕

The Duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, and the Viscount of Zhu, and they jointly concluded a covenant at Duandao. 〔Seventeenth year of Duke Xuan.〕 The Marquis of Jin and Zang, heir apparent of Wei, attacked Qi. 〔Eighteenth year of Duke Xuan.〕

Jisun Xingfu, Zangsun Xu, Shusun Qiaoru, and Gongsun Yingqi led an army to join Xi Ke of Jin, Sun Liangfu of Wei, and Shou, a ducal son of Cao. They fought the Marquis of Qi at An, and the army of Qi suffered a crushing defeat. 〔Second year of Duke Cheng.〕

The Duke met the Viscount of Liu, the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Lesser Zhu at Pingqiu. They jointly concluded a covenant at Pingqiu. The Duke did not participate in the covenant. 〔All in the thirteenth year of Duke Zhao.〕

Shi Yang of Jin, Yue Qili of Song, Beigong Xi of Wei, and representatives of Cao, Zhu, and Teng met at Hu. 〔Twenty-seventh year of Duke Zhao.〕

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
禮記
古者庶子之官治而邦國有倫邦國有倫
而衆鄉方矣
父子篤兄弟睦夫婦和家之肥也大臣法
小臣廉官職相序君臣相正國之肥也
天子以德爲車以樂爲御諸侯以禮相
與大夫以法相序士以信相考百姓以
睦相守天下之肥也是謂大順
若此則周道四達禮樂交通則夫武之遲
===
久不亦宜乎
故謂之有行有行之謂有義有義之謂勇
敢故所貴於勇敢者貴其能以立義也
所貴於立義者貴其有行也所貴於有
行者貴其行禮也故所貴於勇敢者貴
其敢行禮義也
第貳塲
論
聖人天道之自然
punctuated:
禮記

古者，庶子之官治，而邦國有倫；邦國有倫，而衆鄉方矣。

父子篤，兄弟睦，夫婦和，家之肥也；大臣法，小臣廉，官職相序，君臣相正，國之肥也。天子以德爲車，以樂爲御；諸侯以禮相與，大夫以法相序，士以信相考，百姓以睦相守，天下之肥也。是謂大順。

若此，則周道四達，禮樂交通，則夫武之遲久，不亦宜乎？

故謂之有行。有行之謂有義，有義之謂勇敢。故所貴於勇敢者，貴其能以立義也；所貴於立義者，貴其有行也；所貴於有行者，貴其行禮也。故所貴於勇敢者，貴其敢行禮義也。

第貳塲

論

聖人，天道之自然。
translation_en:
Record of Rites (Liji)

In antiquity, when the officials responsible for the sons of the nobility performed their duties properly, relationships within the states were ordered. When relationships within the states were ordered, the people turned toward the proper course.

Devotion between father and son, affection between brothers, and harmony between husband and wife constitute the flourishing of a family. Great ministers observing established standards, lesser ministers maintaining integrity, officials performing their duties in proper order, and ruler and ministers correcting one another constitute the flourishing of a state. The Son of Heaven takes virtue as his carriage and music as his charioteer; the feudal lords deal with one another through ritual propriety; great officers order their relations according to established standards; gentlemen assess one another by their trustworthiness; and the common people sustain one another in harmony. These constitute the flourishing of all under Heaven. This is called the Great Accord.

If this was so—if the Way of Zhou extended in all four directions, and ritual and music circulated everywhere—was it not fitting that the Wu dance should be slow and protracted?

Thus this is called having proper conduct. Having proper conduct means possessing righteousness; possessing righteousness means being courageous. What is valued in courage is its capacity to establish righteousness. What is valued in establishing righteousness is that it entails proper conduct. What is valued in proper conduct is the practice of ritual propriety. Thus what is valued in courage is the daring to put ritual propriety and righteousness into practice.

Second Session

Discourse

The sage is the spontaneous expression of the Way of Heaven.

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
詔誥表内科壹道
擬漢文帝賜天下今年田租之半詔
擬唐以陳叔達爲禮部尚書誥
擬宋胡安國進春秋傳表
判語五條
夜無故入人家
軍民約會詞訟
有事以財請求
官吏聽許財物
===
知情藏匿罪人
第叄場
策五道
問自古帝王之興必有制作以新一代之
耳目洪惟我
朝
英宗睿皇帝大明一統志之作寔籠八表於案
内挫萬里於毫端者也試以全浙之風
俗人物一講之其風俗之見於志者曰
punctuated:
詔誥表内科壹道。
擬漢文帝賜天下今年田租之半詔。
擬唐以陳叔達爲禮部尚書誥。
擬宋胡安國進春秋傳表。

軍民約會詞訟。
有事以財請求。
官吏聽許財物。
知情藏匿罪人。
第叄場
策五道。
問：自古帝王之興，必有制作，以新一代之耳目。洪惟我朝英宗睿皇帝《大明一統志》之作，寔籠八表於案内，挫萬里於毫端者也。試以全浙之風俗人物一講之。其風俗之見於志者曰：
translation_en:
One topic from among edicts, proclamations of appointment, and memorials [?].
Compose an edict in the voice of Emperor Wen of Han remitting half of this year's land tax throughout the realm.
Compose a Tang proclamation appointing Chen Shuda Minister of Rites.
Compose a memorial in the voice of Hu Anguo of the Song presenting his Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu zhuan).

Five legal judgments:
Entering another person's home at night without cause.
Military personnel and civilians arranging to meet to bring litigation.
Seeking a favor in a matter by offering money or property.
Officials and clerks agreeing to accept money or property.
Knowingly harboring an offender.

Third Session
Five policy questions.

Question: Since antiquity, whenever emperors and kings have arisen, they have invariably established institutions and produced works to renew what an age sees and hears. We reverently reflect that the compilation of the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Great Ming (Da Ming yitong zhi) under our dynasty's Emperor Yingzong Rui truly encompassed the eight extremities of the world upon a desk and compressed ten thousand li into the tip of a brush. Discuss this with reference to the customs and notable people of Zhejiang as a whole. Concerning its customs, the gazetteer states: …

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
人性敏慧而習俗工巧曰人和物阜民
貧而番曰知慕文儒頗勤農桑曰儒風
始盛而習俗歸美又有俗勤畊織士知
所學俗悍以寡耿耿好氣者又有君子
尚禮小人勤稼俗重犯法篤志好學者
又有其俗不雜而其人易治其人樸靜
而其俗儉約與夫爭訟少而紡績勤器
用備而秔稻足者可歷舉其地歟其人
物之見于志者有侃然正色而百僚敬
===
憚者有啓沃君心而知無不言者有論
諫甚切而一本仁義者有論疏剴切而
悚動人主者他如起兵勤王志在復國
琴鶴自随卒謚清獻者博學能文尤邃
經術少有高名不屈仕進者與夫引落
帝衣不惜碎首愛惜名器扶持正學發
明中庸之大旨知伊洛之正學者可歷
數其人歟夫班倕之里童子能雕隃秦
青之居耋者能弄吭風俗有係於人之
punctuated: 人性敏慧而習俗工巧，曰「人和物阜，民貧而番」，曰「知慕文儒，頗勤農桑」，曰「儒風始盛，而習俗歸美」。又有「俗勤畊織，士知所學」「俗悍以寡，耿耿好氣」者，又有「君子尚禮，小人勤稼」「俗重犯法，篤志好學」者，又有「其俗不雜，而其人易治」「其人樸靜，而其俗儉約」，與夫「爭訟少而紡績勤，器用備而秔稻足」者，可歷舉其地歟？其人物之見于志者，有侃然正色而百僚敬憚者，有啓沃君心而知無不言者，有論諫甚切而一本仁義者，有論疏剴切而悚動人主者。他如起兵勤王，志在復國，琴鶴自随，卒謚清獻者；博學能文，尤邃經術，少有高名，不屈仕進者；與夫引落帝衣，不惜碎首，愛惜名器，扶持正學，發明中庸之大旨，知伊洛之正學者，可歷數其人歟？夫班倕之里，童子能雕隃；秦青之居，耋者能弄吭。風俗有係於人之
translation_en:
…“The people are intelligent and perceptive, and their customary pursuits display craftsmanship and ingenuity”; “the people live harmoniously and goods are abundant; the people are poor but numerous [?]”; “they know to admire literary learning and Confucian scholars, and are quite diligent in farming and sericulture”; and “Confucian learning has begun to flourish, and customs are tending toward goodness.” There are also places where “the customary occupations are diligent plowing and weaving, and scholars know what they should study,” and where “customs are fierce but few [?], and the people are staunch and spirited”; places where “gentlemen esteem ritual propriety, and common people work diligently at farming,” and where “local custom regards breaking the law as a grave matter, and the people are resolute in their aspirations and devoted to learning”; places where “customs are unmixed, and the people are easy to govern,” and where “the people are simple and quiet, and their customs frugal”; as well as places where “disputes and litigation are few, spinning and weaving are diligently pursued, implements are plentiful, and rice is abundant.” Can you enumerate these places individually?
Among the people recorded in the gazetteer, there were those whose upright bearing and solemn expression inspired respect and awe among all the officials; those who enlightened and nurtured the ruler’s mind, withholding nothing they knew; those whose arguments and remonstrances were most earnest and grounded entirely in benevolence and righteousness; and those whose incisive memorials stirred the sovereign to apprehension. Others raised troops to serve their sovereign, determined to restore the state; traveled with only a zither and a crane, and received the posthumous name Qingxian; were broadly learned and accomplished in writing, with especially profound mastery of the classics; or enjoyed great renown in youth and would not compromise themselves to advance in office. There were also those who pulled down the emperor’s robe, did not shrink from having their heads smashed, guarded the honor of official titles and insignia, upheld orthodox learning, elucidated the central meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean, or understood the orthodox learning of Yi and Luo. Can you enumerate these people individually?
Now, in the home district of Ban and Chui, even young boys could carve [?]; where Qin Qing lived, even men in their eighties could sing. That customs depend upon people’s…

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
變化尚矣諸士子樂育
聖朝菁莪之化百有餘年平居素志所以化導
鄉閭景仰先哲者果以何者為至歟請
陳毋畧
問聖者無不通也故生而知之不思而得
皆所以論聖嘗觀古之所謂聖者而有
疑焉稱堯者曰乃聖乃神矣然臣必試
而後知稱文王者曰緝熈敬止矣然道
猶望而未之見周公非聖人乎仰而思
===
幸而得何其勤且艱若是也孔子之聖
殆無容議姑以其細者言之萍實之對
商羊之答土羵之辨鉅骨之考可謂無
不通矣然問禮問官問樂學琴禘之說
則曰不知軍旅之事則曰未學封禪之
書讀之而不能盡通也聖人固如是乎
夫聖人而亦有所不通則其為聖亦易
矣聖而猶有待於學則學而知之者亦
可以謂之聖乎試言所以希聖之學
punctuated:
變化尚矣。諸士子樂育聖朝菁莪之化百有餘年，平居素志，所以化導鄉閭、景仰先哲者，果以何者為至歟？請陳毋畧。
問：聖者無不通也，故生而知之、不思而得，皆所以論聖。嘗觀古之所謂聖者，而有疑焉。稱堯者曰：「乃聖乃神」矣，然臣必試而後知；稱文王者曰：「緝熈敬止」矣，然道猶望而未之見。周公非聖人乎？仰而思，幸而得，何其勤且艱若是也！孔子之聖，殆無容議。姑以其細者言之，萍實之對、商羊之答、土羵之辨、鉅骨之考，可謂無不通矣。然問禮、問官、問樂、學琴，禘之說則曰不知，軍旅之事則曰未學，封禪之書讀之而不能盡通也。聖人固如是乎？夫聖人而亦有所不通，則其為聖亦易矣。聖而猶有待於學，則學而知之者亦可以謂之聖乎？試言所以希聖之學。
translation_en:
…such transformation has long been esteemed. You candidates have enjoyed the nurturing influence of our sagely dynasty, whose cultivation of talent, celebrated in the “Luxuriant Southernwood” ode, has continued for more than a hundred years. In your longstanding aspirations in everyday life, what do you regard as the highest means of morally guiding your home communities and emulating the worthies of the past? Please explain without omission.
Question: A sage understands everything. Thus, being born with knowledge and attaining understanding without deliberation are both descriptions of sagehood. Yet, on considering those called sages in antiquity, I have found grounds for doubt. Those who praised Yao said that he was “sagely and divine”; nevertheless, he had to test his ministers before knowing them. Those who praised King Wen said that he was “continuously luminous and abiding in reverence”; nevertheless, he looked toward the Way as though he had not yet seen it. Was the Duke of Zhou not a sage? He looked upward in thought and, by good fortune, attained understanding. Why did this require such diligence and difficulty? The sagehood of Confucius surely admits of no dispute. To speak only of lesser matters: his explanation of the floating fruit, his answer concerning the shangyang bird, his identification of the earth sheep, and his investigation of the enormous bone might be said to show that he understood everything. Yet he inquired about ritual, official offices, and music, and studied the zither. Concerning the explanation of the di sacrifice, he said that he did not know; concerning military affairs, he said that he had not studied them. He read writings on the feng and shan sacrifices but could not fully comprehend them. Is this indeed what a sage is like? If even a sage has things he does not understand, then becoming a sage would seem easy. If even a sage must depend on learning, may those who acquire knowledge through learning also be called sages? Explain the learning through which one may aspire to sagehood.

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
問古之用賢無定法惟其人而已有非常
之材者固不可以常法遇之莘野之聘
傅巖之求渭濱之載姑置勿論降至西
漢武宣號稱得人然當時賢臣名士往
往有拔之芻牧之中而表之卿相之上
者時論不以為嫌何後世之不然耶夫
大臣以人事君豈不欲明揚俊民以輔
邦國顧知人則哲自古為難然則當用
人之柄者其甄奇錄異如李肅山濤乎
===
抑慎守年資如崔亮裴光庭乎將舉先
德行如牛弘推奬法吏如戴胄乎崔祐
甫除吏八百未免有舉多親故之譏常
衮盡公守法未免有賢愚同滯之誚又
果將何所適從乎習俗之薄議論之多
欲望得人於微陋之中而成功於繩墨
之外亦難矣何施何為而可以臻得人
之盛願為我言之
問兵者國之大事聖人不得已而用之也
punctuated:
問：古之用賢，無定法，惟其人而已。有非常之材者，固不可以常法遇之。莘野之聘、傅巖之求、渭濱之載，姑置勿論。降至西漢，武、宣號稱得人，然當時賢臣名士，往往有拔之芻牧之中而表之卿相之上者，時論不以為嫌，何後世之不然耶？夫大臣以人事君，豈不欲明揚俊民以輔邦國？顧知人則哲，自古為難。然則當用人之柄者，其甄奇錄異，如李肅、山濤乎？抑慎守年資，如崔亮、裴光庭乎？將舉先德行，如牛弘；推奬法吏，如戴胄乎？崔祐甫除吏八百，未免有舉多親故之譏；常衮盡公守法，未免有賢愚同滯之誚。又果將何所適從乎？習俗之薄，議論之多，欲望得人於微陋之中，而成功於繩墨之外，亦難矣。何施何為，而可以臻得人之盛？願為我言之。

問：兵者，國之大事，聖人不得已而用之也。
translation_en:
Question: In antiquity there was no fixed method for employing worthy men; everything depended on the individual. Men of extraordinary talent certainly could not be treated by ordinary rules. Let us set aside the invitation issued in the fields of Shen, the search at Fu Yan, and the carriage ride from the banks of the Wei. Coming down to the Western Han, Emperors Wu and Xuan were renowned for obtaining able men. Worthy ministers and eminent men of that time were often raised from among grass-cutters and herdsmen and exalted above high ministers and chief ministers. Contemporary opinion found nothing objectionable in this. Why has it been otherwise in later ages?

Great ministers serve their ruler by finding men for him: how could they not wish to bring outstanding men to prominence to assist the state? Yet discerning men requires wisdom, and this has been difficult since antiquity. Should those who wield the power of appointment, then, select exceptional men and recruit unusual talent, like Li Su and Shan Tao? Or should they scrupulously adhere to seniority, like Cui Liang and Pei Guangting? Should they give precedence to moral conduct in recommending men, like Niu Hong, or promote officials versed in law, like Dai Zhou? Cui Youfu appointed eight hundred officials, yet could not escape criticism that many of his nominees were relatives and old acquaintances. Chang Gun acted with complete impartiality and observed the rules, yet could not escape the reproach that worthy and foolish alike were held back. Which course, then, should one actually follow?

With customs debased and critical opinions so numerous, it is indeed difficult to hope to find able men among the humble and obscure and achieve success beyond the bounds of established rules. What measures and actions could bring about an abundance of able men in service? Please explain this to me.

Question: Warfare is a great affair of state. The sage resorts to it only when compelled by necessity. …

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
商周之時若伊尹鳴條之役呂望牧野
之師其神武不殺見之湯牧二誓不可
尚已戰國以還善言兵者莫如孫武其
法後世因之亦猶方圓之不能過乎規
矩也試舉一二與諸士子商確之其法
曰將能而君不御者勝上下同欲者勝
孰用之而果能取勝乎曰用間者因其
鄉人而用之因其官人而用之孰取勝
而果由用間乎曰屈人之兵而非戰與
===
不戰而屈人之兵合其法而成功者誰
歟曰以飽待飢以佚待勞循其法而得
捷者誰歟厲於廊廟之上以誅其事興
漢之迹可考也然以老將而曰兵難遙
度兵聞拙速破羌之迹可稽也然以老
臣而曰吾緩之自當携貳是果出於一
法歟裨將棄師若可斬也宥之而不一
刁斗不擊若可襲也而士卒樂爲之用
是又不用法者歟我
punctuated: 商周之時，若伊尹鳴條之役、呂望牧野之師，其神武不殺，見之湯牧二誓，不可尚已。戰國以還，善言兵者莫如孫武，其法後世因之，亦猶方圓之不能過乎規矩也。試舉一二，與諸士子商確之。其法曰：「將能而君不御者勝，上下同欲者勝。」孰用之而果能取勝乎？曰：「用間者，因其鄉人而用之，因其官人而用之。」孰取勝而果由用間乎？曰：「屈人之兵而非戰」，與「不戰而屈人之兵」，合其法而成功者誰歟？曰：「以飽待飢，以佚待勞。」循其法而得捷者誰歟？厲於廊廟之上，以誅其事，興漢之迹可考也；然以老將而曰：「兵難遙度。」兵聞拙速，破羌之迹可稽也；然以老臣而曰：「吾緩之，自當携貳。」是果出於一法歟？裨將棄師，若可斬也，宥之而不一；刁斗不擊，若可襲也，而士卒樂爲之用。是又不用法者歟？我
translation_en:
In the Shang and Zhou periods, in such campaigns as Yi Yin’s battle at Mingtiao and Lü Wang’s expedition to Muye, their divine martial prowess without killing is manifest in the two oaths, the Oath of Tang and the Oath at Mu. It could not be surpassed. From the Warring States onward, none excelled Sun Wu in discussing warfare. Later generations followed his methods, just as circles and squares cannot depart from the compass and the carpenter’s square. Let us raise one or two points for discussion with you candidates.

His methods state: “Those whose general is capable and whose ruler does not constrain him will win; those whose superiors and subordinates share the same desires will win.” Who employed these methods and actually achieved victory? He says: “In employing spies, use people from the enemy’s own locality; use the enemy’s own officials.” Whose victory actually resulted from employing spies? He says: “Subdue the enemy’s troops without fighting,” and “Without fighting, subdue the enemy’s troops.” Who achieved success in accordance with these methods? He says: “With well-fed troops await the hungry; with rested troops await the weary.” Who followed these methods and won?

To exert authority within the court and thereby punish their deeds [?]—the events surrounding the rise of the Han can be examined. 有四一曰水利二曰鹽課三曰銀冶四

translation_en:
…the dynasty’s peaceful and stable government is without precedent in antiquity. Yet the ancients admonished us not to forget danger in times of security. If you candidates should be entrusted with military command, whom would you take as your model for deploying surprise forces amid the wine vessels and sacrificial stands of court, and sweeping away savage foes from within the command tent? Tell me, I pray, withholding nothing.

Question: The affairs of government throughout the realm are numerous. Taking just the Two Zhe regions, there are four urgent concerns: first, water management; second, the salt tax; third, silver mining and smelting; fourth, maritime affairs. Reckoning the land irrigated by the various lakes, their waters can readily serve hundreds or thousands of mu. Yet nearly half have now been filled in and turned into farmland. Proposals to repair and dredge them unsettle the powerful local families; leaving them unchecked means that they become increasingly filled in. How can irrigation be restored without provoking resentment among the people? Reckoning the proceeds from salt at the various salterns, how could the annual total be merely several tens of millions of strings of cash? Yet these proceeds are now almost entirely dissipated in wasteful expenditure. Proposals to organize their management inconvenience the powerful; leaving matters unattended means ever greater losses. How can merchants enjoy sufficiency while the state also prospers? text:
四書
自天子以至於庶人壹是皆以脩身為本
翁健之
同考試官訓導梁批大學一題連日披閱殊無可人意者忽
得此作良玉出而燕石下矣
同考試官訓導王批理明辭健知所歸重宜表出之
考試官訓導桑批認理真遣辭暢
考試官教授林批體貼註義脫去陳言佳作也
大學之結八條目必揭其要以示人焉夫大學
===
之道莫要於脩身也然非揭言以示人孰從而
知其然哉且大學之綱領有三而條目則八焉
八者何格致誠正脩齊治平是已然八者之中
而脩身為要人可不知所重乎故上自天子而
下至庶人貴賤雖不同也然均之為人而壹是
皆以脩身為本焉譬之網而提其綱也否則推
之而有所不準奚可乎哉尊卑雖有異也然均
之為學而一切皆以脩身為本焉譬之裘而挈
其領也否則動之而有所不化又可乎哉物欲

四書

自天子以至於庶人，壹是皆以脩身為本。

翁健之

同考試官訓導梁批：「大學一題，連日披閱，殊無可人意者。忽得此作，良玉出而燕石下矣。」

同考試官訓導王批：「理明辭健，知所歸重，宜表出之。」

大學之結八條目，必揭其要以示人焉。夫大學之道，莫要於脩身也。然非揭言以示人，孰從而知其然哉？且大學之綱領有三，而條目則八焉。八者何？格、致、誠、正、脩、齊、治、平，是已。然八者之中，而脩身為要，人可不知所重乎？故上自天子而下至庶人，貴賤雖不同也，然均之為人，而壹是皆以脩身為本焉。譬之網而提其綱也，否則推之而有所不準，奚可乎哉？尊卑雖有異也，然均之為學，而一切皆以脩身為本焉。譬之裘而挈其領也，否則動之而有所不化，又可乎哉？物欲

“From the Son of Heaven down to the common people, all alike take cultivation of the self as the foundation.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor: “Clear in principle and vigorous in expression. He knows where the emphasis belongs. This deserves to be singled out.”

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Closely attuned to the meaning of the commentary and free of stale expressions. An excellent composition.”

In concluding its account of the eight steps, the Great Learning necessarily brings their essential point to the fore to instruct people. In the Way of the Great Learning, nothing is more essential than cultivating the self. Yet unless this is explicitly stated to instruct people, how could anyone come to understand that it is so? Now the Great Learning has three guiding principles and eight steps. What are the eight? Investigating things, extending knowledge, making the intentions sincere, rectifying the mind, cultivating the self, regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the world: these are they. Yet among these eight, cultivating the self is the essential point. Can people fail to know where the emphasis lies?

Thus, from the Son of Heaven above down to the common people below, although their noble or humble status differs, they are equally human, and all alike take cultivation of the self as the foundation. It is like lifting a net by its main cord. Otherwise, when one extends one's efforts outward, some things will fail to conform to the standard. How could that be acceptable? Although their high or low standing differs, they are equally engaged in learning, and all without exception take cultivation of the self as the foundation. title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
格知欲致皆其脩之之功意欲誠心欲正悉其
脩之之實自身而后家國所以齊治者孰不於
我乎是準自家國而后天下所以平者孰不於
我乎是化是則吾身一脩而大學之能事以畢
所繫之重若此身乎身乎其可以不脩乎大學
結八條目而揭此為言其示人之意深矣大抵
人之一身萬化之本原故人能脩身則家國天
下之事業隨之此正明德之事而新民之機實
大學之要道也孟子他日亦曰君子之守脩其
===
身而天下平孔孟相傳心法於此可見
莫春者春服既成冠者五六人童子六七人
浴乎沂風乎舞雩詠而歸夫子喟然嘆曰
吾與點也
孫鑰
同考試官訓導張 批 塲中作此題者類多陳言獨此篇
能化腐為新殆猶園林變而春則生輝者也
同考試官訓導陸 批 說堯許由黙處他春意自見語亦
同考試官教諭李 批 形容曾點所樂如親見其人

格，知欲致，皆其脩之之功；意欲誠，心欲正，悉其脩之之實。自身而后家國，所以齊治者，孰不於我乎是準？自家國而后天下，所以平者，孰不於我乎是化？是則吾身一脩，而大學之能事以畢。所繫之重若此，身乎！身乎！其可以不脩乎？《大學》結八條目而揭此為言，其示人之意深矣！大抵人之一身，萬化之本原，故人能脩身，則家國天下之事業隨之。此正明德之事，而新民之機，實大學之要道也。孟子他日亦曰：「君子之守，脩其身而天下平。」孔孟相傳心法，於此可見。

「莫春者，春服既成，冠者五六人，童子六七人，浴乎沂，風乎舞雩，詠而歸。」夫子喟然嘆曰：「吾與點也！」

孫鑰

同考試官訓導陸批：說堯許由黙處他春意自見，語亦。

同考試官教諭李批：形容曾點所樂，如親見其人。
translation_en:
…to investigate things and extend knowledge: these are all the work of cultivating oneself. To make the intentions sincere and rectify the mind: these are all the substance of that cultivation. From oneself onward to the family and state, what means of ordering the family and governing the state does not take its standard from oneself? From the family and state onward to all under Heaven, what means of bringing peace does not derive its transforming influence from oneself? Thus, once I have cultivated myself, all that the Great Learning can accomplish is fulfilled. So much depends upon it! This person of ours, this person of ours—can we leave it uncultivated? In concluding its eight stages, the Great Learning singles this out for emphasis. Profound indeed is its intention in instructing people! Broadly speaking, each person's self is the source of all transformation. Thus, if people can cultivate themselves, achievements in the family, state, and all under Heaven follow. This is precisely the work of manifesting luminous virtue and the mainspring of renewing the people; it is truly the essential way of the Great Learning. Mencius also said on another occasion: “What the gentleman holds fast to is this: cultivate oneself, and all under Heaven will be at peace.” Here we can see the teaching of the mind transmitted from Confucius to Mencius.

“In late spring, when the spring clothes are ready, with five or six capped young men and six or seven boys, I would bathe in the Yi River, take the breeze at the Rain Dance Terrace, and return singing.” The Master sighed deeply and said: “I am with Dian!”

Sun Yue 孫鑰

text:
考試官訓導桑批氣昌
考試官教授林批理明語新錄之以式後學
賢者言志聖人嘆而許之也夫志乃心之所之
也聖人因賢者言志而嘆許之得非有契於心
乎昔子路曾點冉有公西華侍坐夫子問志有
及於點故對之如此謂夫時維三月序屬莫春
斯時也景物熈明春服旣備長而已冠者五六
人焉未冠而爲童子者六七人焉相與盥濯乎
沂水之濵娯溫泉之觱沸相與乘凉于舞雩之
===
下挹惠風之暢和載歌載詠而伴奐爾游襟懷
爲之一洗言還言歸而優游爾休物我爲之兩
忘點之志如此而已夫子於是喟然嘆曰乗斯
時也與斯人也寓斯地也樂斯樂也位不出其
所居事惟在於日用見高一世無舍己爲人之
意彼規規於事爲之末者其氣象不侔矣吾非
點與而孰與乎胸次悠然有對時育物之妙彼
屑屑於事功之小者其規模自異矣吾非點許
而誰許乎噫夫子進曾點而激三子之意至矣

考試官訓導桑批：氣昌。
考試官教授林批：理明語新，錄之以式後學。
賢者言志，聖人嘆而許之也。夫志乃心之所之也，聖人因賢者言志而嘆許之，得非有契於心乎？昔子路、曾點、冉有、公西華侍坐，夫子問志，有及於點，故對之如此。謂夫時維三月，序屬莫春，斯時也，景物熈明，春服旣備，長而已冠者五六人焉，未冠而爲童子者六七人焉，相與盥濯乎沂水之濵，娯溫泉之觱沸；相與乘凉于舞雩之下，挹惠風之暢和。載歌載詠而伴奐爾游，襟懷爲之一洗；言還言歸而優游爾休，物我爲之兩忘。點之志如此而已。夫子於是喟然嘆曰：「乗斯時也，與斯人也，寓斯地也，樂斯樂也，位不出其所居，事惟在於日用，見高一世，無舍己爲人之意。彼規規於事爲之末者，其氣象不侔矣，吾非點與而孰與乎？胸次悠然，有對時育物之妙，彼屑屑於事功之小者，其規模自異矣，吾非點許而誰許乎？」噫！夫子進曾點而激三子之意至矣！
translation_en:
Examiner Sang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The spirit is vigorous.”
Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “The principles are clear and the language fresh. It is recorded here as a model for later students.”
The worthy man expressed his aspiration, and the sage sighed in approval. Aspiration is the direction in which the heart moves. When the sage sighed in approval upon hearing the worthy man express his aspiration, was it not because something accorded with his own heart? Formerly, Zilu, Zeng Dian, Ran You, and Gongxi Hua sat in attendance upon the Master. The Master asked about their aspirations, and his question reached Dian, who therefore answered in this way: “It is the third month, the season of late spring. At this time, the scenery is bright and mild, and spring clothes are ready. With five or six adults who have undergone capping, and six or seven boys not yet capped, we wash together on the banks of the Yi River, enjoying the bubbling warm springs. Together we take the cool air below the Rain Dance Terrace, drawing in the gentle, soothing breeze. Singing and chanting, we wander at ease, our hearts washed clean; returning home, we rest at leisure, forgetting both the external world and ourselves. Such, and nothing more, is my aspiration.”
The Master thereupon sighed deeply and said: “To take advantage of this season, join these companions, spend time in this place, and delight in this pleasure: he does not step beyond his station, and his concerns lie entirely in everyday life. His insight rises above his age, with no intention of abandoning his own cultivation for the sake of others’ regard. Those narrowly absorbed in the lesser details of practical affairs cannot match his bearing. If I do not side with Dian, with whom shall I side? His heart is at ease, possessing the subtle capacity to accord with the seasons and nurture all things. Those busily occupied with petty accomplishments differ from him in the very scope of their outlook. If I do not approve of Dian, whom shall I approve?” Ah! Profound indeed was the Master’s intention in commending Zeng Dian and spurring on the other three disciples!

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄

感於用舍行藏之際故一聆點也之言適與意

邪昔孟子序君子之樂至此謂夫心者一身之

Yet consider this aspiration of Zeng Dian: he was almost like one of the people of Getian or Wuhuai, the rulers of remote antiquity. Looking back at the undertakings proposed by the other three disciples, was the distance between them merely tenfold or a hundredfold? Our Master's aspiration was to bring peace to the aged, cherish the young, and be trustworthy toward friends. His intention, too, was surely to share with everyone in the world the pleasure of bathing in the Yi River and enjoying the breeze at the Rain Dance Altar. Yet, constrained by his times, he was then deeply moved by the question of serving when employed and withdrawing when set aside. Thus, as soon as he heard Dian's words, they accorded perfectly with his own thoughts, and he sighed without even realizing it. Here one may discern a spirit as expansive as Heaven and Earth.
“Looking up, to have no shame before Heaven; looking down, to have no shame before others.”

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
棄天矣揆之方寸寧不有愧於天邪必巳無不
克而天之所以與我者無斲喪之非則人泯天
定矣日用之間靜焉而與天俱動焉而與天合
方寸盎然仰而在上天雖高也吾何愧於天哉
使人能盡之而我獨梏亡之則非人矣揣之靈
臺寧不有怍於人邪必巳無不克而我之所得
於天者無梏亡之失則欲淨理還矣日用之間
人能知而我亦能知人能行而我亦能行靈臺
泰然俯而在下人雖眾也吾何怍於人哉是則
===
===
仰不愧於天則天即我而我亦天矣俯不怍於
人則我即人而人亦我矣俯仰無歉心廣體胖
克巳之功其大如此君子之樂豈外於是哉抑
考孟子此章論君子之三樂上文言父母俱存
兄弟無故至此以是為言下文又言得天下英
才而教育之先儒謂此三樂者一係於天一係
於人其可自致者惟不愧不怍而巳學者必於
是而有得焉庶可行道於家而傳道於来世也
易
punctuated:
棄天矣，揆之方寸，寧不有愧於天邪？必巳無不克，而天之所以與我者無斲喪之非，則人泯天定矣。日用之間，靜焉而與天俱，動焉而與天合，方寸盎然，仰而在上，天雖高也，吾何愧於天哉？使人能盡之，而我獨梏亡之，則非人矣。揣之靈臺，寧不有怍於人邪？必巳無不克，而我之所得於天者無梏亡之失，則欲淨理還矣。日用之間，人能知而我亦能知，人能行而我亦能行，靈臺泰然，俯而在下，人雖眾也，吾何怍於人哉？是則仰不愧於天，則天即我而我亦天矣；俯不怍於人，則我即人而人亦我矣。俯仰無歉，心廣體胖，克巳之功其大如此，君子之樂豈外於是哉？抑考孟子此章論君子之三樂，上文言父母俱存、兄弟無故，至此以是為言，下文又言得天下英才而教育之。先儒謂此三樂者，一係於天，一係於人，其可自致者惟不愧不怍而巳。學者必於是而有得焉，庶可行道於家而傳道於来世也。

易
translation_en:
… to abandon Heaven. Examining this within one's own heart, how could one fail to feel shame before Heaven? Only when the self has been thoroughly overcome, and what Heaven has bestowed upon me has suffered no wrongful injury or destruction, are human desires extinguished and the heavenly principle firmly established. In daily life, in stillness I abide with Heaven, and in action I accord with Heaven; my heart brims with vitality. Looking upward, though Heaven above is high, what cause have I for shame before it? If others can fully realize this endowment, while I alone fetter and destroy it, then I am no longer human. Searching the inner sanctuary of my mind, how could I fail to feel shame before others? Only when the self has been thoroughly overcome, and what I have received from Heaven has suffered no loss through constraint and destruction, are desires cleared away and principle restored. In daily life, what others can understand, I too can understand; what others can carry out, I too can carry out. My mind is at peace. Looking downward, though the people below are many, what cause have I for shame before them? Thus, when I look up without shame before Heaven, Heaven is myself and I too am Heaven; when I look down without shame before others, I am others and others too are myself. With no misgivings whether looking up or down, the mind is spacious and the body at ease. Such is the greatness of the achievement of overcoming the self. Could the gentleman's joy lie outside this?

Furthermore, consider this chapter of the Mengzi, which discusses the gentleman's three joys. The preceding passage speaks of having both parents alive and one's brothers free from misfortune; at this point it speaks of being without shame; and the following passage speaks of obtaining the outstanding talents of the realm and educating them. Earlier Confucian scholars said that, of these three joys, one depends on Heaven and one depends on other people; the only one attainable through one's own efforts is to be without shame before Heaven or others. Students must gain a personal understanding of this, so that they may practice the Way within their families and transmit it to future generations.

Book of Changes

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
首出庶物萬國咸寧
張輔
同考試官訓導梁批辭簡理明深得本義之旨録出
同考試官訓導王批發揮聖人彖傳之意无遺必熟於易者
考試官訓導桑批得㫖
考試官教授林批易義似此者不多
聖人出於上天下成其治此聖人之利貞也盖
治由聖人而成也今焉髙出於上而天下焉有
不治者哉乾彖言聖人之利貞如此謂夫聖人
具乾剛之體妙乾元之用應時而出疆宇賴之
以統御撫運而興民物託之以依歸正五位以
凝命卓乎其無與倫也乗六龍以御天巍乎其
莫與並也乾德以之而廣布天道以之而大行
所謂飛龍在天者此其時乎由是萬國雖大凡
沐其德者皆有以順其性萬邦雖廣凡被其澤
者皆有以遂其生春臺玉燭之中熈熈乎其自
如也光天化日之下皡皡乎其自若也所謂天
下化成者此其驗乎是則首出庶物猶乾道之
punctuated:
首出庶物，萬國咸寧。
張輔
同考試官訓導梁批：辭簡理明，深得本義之旨，録出。
同考試官訓導王批：發揮聖人彖傳之意无遺，必熟於易者。
考試官訓導桑批：得㫖。
考試官教授林批：易義似此者不多。
聖人出於上，天下成其治，此聖人之利貞也。盖治由聖人而成也，今焉髙出於上，而天下焉有不治者哉？乾彖言聖人之利貞如此，謂夫聖人具乾剛之體，妙乾元之用，應時而出，疆宇賴之以統御；撫運而興，民物託之以依歸。正五位以凝命，卓乎其無與倫也；乗六龍以御天，巍乎其莫與並也。乾德以之而廣布，天道以之而大行。所謂飛龍在天者，此其時乎？由是萬國雖大，凡沐其德者皆有以順其性；萬邦雖廣，凡被其澤者皆有以遂其生。春臺玉燭之中，熈熈乎其自如也；光天化日之下，皡皡乎其自若也。所謂天下化成者，此其驗乎？是則首出庶物，猶乾道之
translation_en:
“He emerges above the multitude of beings, and the myriad states are all at peace.”
Zhang Fu
Associate Examiner Liang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Concise in expression and clear in principle, this thoroughly captures the purport of the Original Meaning [of the Book of Changes]. Selected for transcription.”
Associate Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “It expounds the sage’s meaning in the Commentary on the Judgments without omission. Its author must be well versed in the Book of Changes.”
Examiner Sang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “It grasps the purport.”
Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “Few essays on the Book of Changes are like this.”
The sage emerges in the highest position, and order is brought to completion throughout the world: this is the sage’s ‘benefit and correctness.’ For order is accomplished through the sage. Now that he stands high above, how could the world fail to be well governed? Such is what the Commentary on the Judgment for Qian says of the sage’s benefit and correctness. It means that the sage embodies Qian’s firmness and wondrously exercises its primal creative power. He emerges in response to the times, and the realm relies on him for unified governance; he rises in accordance with the course of destiny, and the people and all beings entrust themselves to his protection. He takes his proper place in the fifth position to secure the mandate, standing so eminently that none can compare with him. He rides the six dragons to steer through Heaven, so lofty that none can equal him. Through him Qian’s virtue spreads far and wide, and Heaven’s Way prevails extensively. Is this not the time spoken of as ‘the flying dragon in Heaven’?
Thus, vast though the myriad states may be, all who bathe in his virtue are enabled to follow their own natures; extensive though the myriad domains may be, all who receive his bounty are enabled to fulfill their lives. Amid the joys of the spring terrace and the harmonious seasons, they are contentedly at ease; beneath the bright heavens and the transforming sun, they are expansively free and untroubled. Is this not the proof of what is called ‘the transformation of the world brought to completion’? Thus, ‘emerging above the multitude of beings’ is like the Way of Qian’s …

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
變化也萬國咸寧猶萬物之各正性命而保合
太和也聖人得天位行天道而天下成其治如
此豈非與天同一利貞也歟抑論伏羲畫乾之
卦文王繫以元亨利貞之辭矣至吾夫子傳彖
又析為四德以發明之在天道如此在聖人亦
如此也有志於易者由己以考諸聖由聖以驗
諸天斯理尤有以待乎人也故曰君子以自彊
不息
乾知大始坤作成物乾以易知坤以簡能易
===
則易知簡則易從易知則有親易從則有
功有親則可久有功則可大可久則賢人
之德可大則賢人之業易簡而天下之理
得矣天下之理得而成位乎其中矣
翁健之
同考試官訓導梁 批 題雖平易意有照應此作得之
同考試官訓導王 批 於人兼體乾坤處發明親切可取
考試官訓導桑 批 易卷中之錚錚者
考試官教授林 批 簡潔
punctuated:
變化也，萬國咸寧猶萬物之各正性命而保合太和也。聖人得天位，行天道，而天下成其治如此，豈非與天同一利貞也歟？抑論伏羲畫乾之卦，文王繫以元亨利貞之辭矣。至吾夫子傳彖，又析為四德以發明之。在天道如此，在聖人亦如此也。有志於易者，由己以考諸聖，由聖以驗諸天，斯理尤有以待乎人也。故曰：「君子以自彊不息。」

乾知大始，坤作成物。乾以易知，坤以簡能。易則易知，簡則易從；易知則有親，易從則有功；有親則可久，有功則可大；可久則賢人之德，可大則賢人之業。易簡而天下之理得矣，天下之理得而成位乎其中矣。

翁健之

同考試官訓導梁批：題雖平易，意有照應，此作得之。
同考試官訓導王批：於人兼體乾坤處，發明親切，可取。
考試官訓導桑批：易卷中之錚錚者。
考試官教授林批：簡潔。
translation_en:
…the transformations. The myriad states all enjoying peace is like the myriad things each attaining their proper nature and allotted destiny, and preserving their union in supreme harmony. The sage obtains Heaven’s position and carries out Heaven’s Way, bringing the world to such good order: is this not to share with Heaven the same qualities of benefit and steadfast correctness? Furthermore, Fuxi drew the hexagram Qian, and King Wen attached to it the words “origin, success, benefit, and steadfast correctness.” When our Master composed the Commentary on the Judgments, he further distinguished these as four virtues to elucidate them. This is so in Heaven’s Way, and likewise in the sage. Those intent on studying the Book of Changes should proceed from themselves to examine these principles in the sages, and from the sages to verify them in Heaven. These principles thus still await realization by human beings. Hence it says: “The gentleman strengthens himself without ceasing.”

Qian presides over the great beginning; Kun brings things to completion. Qian presides through ease; Kun accomplishes through simplicity. What is easy is easy to understand; what is simple is easy to follow. Being easy to understand brings affinity; being easy to follow brings achievement. Affinity makes endurance possible; achievement makes greatness possible. The capacity to endure is the virtue of the worthy person; the capacity for greatness is the undertaking of the worthy person. Through ease and simplicity, the principles of all under Heaven are grasped. Once these principles are grasped, one establishes one’s position in their midst.

Weng Jianzhi

Associate Examiner Liang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Although the topic is straightforward, its ideas echo and respond to one another. This composition captures that.”
Associate Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Its elucidation of how human beings embody both Qian and Kun is apt and direct, and merits approval.”
Examiner Sang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “One of the outstanding scripts on the Book of Changes.”
Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “Concise and clear.”

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
大傳論乾坤之理分見於天地人兼體之可參
乎天地蓋乾坤之理不外乎易簡而已人能兼
體之則由賢而聖而參乎天地矣聖人得不推
言至是哉昔大傳聖人承上文男女而言乾坤
之理謂夫乾道固成男也而凡物屬乎陽者
成象以為始皆乾以主之坤道固成女也而凡
物屬乎陰者效法以自生皆坤以成之蓋乾
健而動即其所知便能始物而无所難故為以
易而知大始坤順而靜凡其所能皆從乎陽而
===
不自作故為以簡而能成物乾坤之理分見於
天地如此人之所為如乾之易則其心明白而
人易知如坤之簡則其事要約而人易從易知
則與之同心者多故有親易從則與之協力者
眾故有功有親則一於內故可久有功則兼於
外故可大可久則賢人之德而得於已也可大
則賢人之業而成於事也自可久而極其易則
天下理之易者盡得而无遺自可大而極其簡
則天下理之簡者全體而无外天下之理既得
punctuated:
大傳論乾坤之理分見於天地，人兼體之，可參乎天地。蓋乾坤之理不外乎易簡而已，人能兼體之，則由賢而聖，而參乎天地矣。聖人得不推言至是哉？
昔大傳聖人承上文男女而言乾坤之理，謂夫乾道固成男也，而凡物屬乎陽者，成象以為始，皆乾以主之；坤道固成女也，而凡物屬乎陰者，效法以自生，皆坤以成之。蓋乾健而動，即其所知，便能始物而无所難，故為以易而知大始；坤順而靜，凡其所能，皆從乎陽而不自作，故為以簡而能成物。乾坤之理分見於天地如此。
人之所為如乾之易，則其心明白而人易知；如坤之簡，則其事要約而人易從。易知，則與之同心者多，故有親；易從，則與之協力者眾，故有功。有親則一於內，故可久；有功則兼於外，故可大。可久則賢人之德，而得於已也；可大則賢人之業，而成於事也。自可久而極其易，則天下理之易者盡得而无遺；自可大而極其簡，則天下理之簡者全體而无外。天下之理既得
translation_en:
The Great Commentary discusses how the principles of Qian and Kun manifest themselves separately in Heaven and Earth, and how human beings, by embodying both, can stand alongside Heaven and Earth as a third power. The principles of Qian and Kun amount to nothing beyond ease and simplicity. If people can embody both, they can advance from worthiness to sagehood and stand alongside Heaven and Earth. How could the sage refrain from extending his discussion to this point?
In the Great Commentary, the sage takes up the preceding passage about male and female to explain the principles of Qian and Kun. His meaning is that the way of Qian indeed produces the male, while all things belonging to yang take on images as their beginning, with Qian presiding over them all. The way of Kun indeed produces the female, while all things belonging to yin follow the pattern to come into being, with Kun bringing them all to completion. Qian is vigorous and active: through what it governs, it can initiate things without difficulty. Hence it is said to govern the great beginning through ease. Kun is compliant and still: in everything it can accomplish, it follows yang and does not act on its own initiative. Hence it is said to bring things to completion through simplicity. Such is the separate manifestation of the principles of Qian and Kun in Heaven and Earth.
If a person's conduct resembles the ease of Qian, his mind is clear and others readily understand him. If it resembles the simplicity of Kun, his affairs are concise and others readily follow him. When he is readily understood, many share his purposes; hence he gains close attachments. When he is readily followed, many cooperate with him; hence he achieves results. Close attachments bring unity within, making endurance possible; achievements extend his reach outward, making greatness possible. What can endure constitutes the worthy person's virtue, attained within himself. What can become great constitutes the worthy person's undertaking, accomplished in affairs. Proceeding from the capacity to endure and bringing ease to its utmost, he fully grasps all that is easy in the principles of the world, leaving nothing out. Proceeding from the capacity for greatness and bringing simplicity to its utmost, he wholly embodies all that is simple in the principles of the world, excluding nothing. Once the principles of the world have been grasped…

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
則人道盡矣殆見天以易而知始於上吾以易
成位乎中而上與天參也地以簡而作成於下
吾以簡成位乎中而下與地參也體道之極功
聖人之能事至是尚何加哉嗟夫易簡之於易
理至矣乾坤生萬物聖人參兩儀一於是而已
世之末學顧乃險阻其心煩擾其行則於理已
相背馳而況於希賢乎況於希聖乎況於希天
乎必知此然後可以語易
書
惟事事乃其有備有備無患
孫鑰
同考試官訓導張 批 憲天聰明之意正如此
同考試官訓導陸 批 以未然將然字立說文思亦新傅
說告君之意焯然在目也本房優選吾於小卜之
同考試官教諭李 批 寫出思患豫防之意鑿鑿可行佳士也
考試官訓導桑 批 詞整意足書卷之最者
考試官教授林 批 發明傅說告君之意殆盡
惟能防患於未然斯能免患於將然夫思患豫
punctuated:
則人道盡矣。殆見天以易而知始於上，吾以易成位乎中，而上與天參也；地以簡而作成於下，吾以簡成位乎中，而下與地參也。體道之極功，聖人之能事，至是尚何加哉！嗟夫！易簡之於易，理至矣。乾坤生萬物，聖人參兩儀，一於是而已。世之末學，顧乃險阻其心，煩擾其行，則於理已相背馳，而況於希賢乎？況於希聖乎？況於希天乎？必知此，然後可以語易。

書
惟事事乃其有備，有備無患。
孫鑰

同考試官訓導張批：憲天聰明之意，正如此。
同考試官訓導陸批：以未然、將然字立說，文思亦新。傅說告君之意，焯然在目也。本房優選，吾於小卜之。
同考試官教諭李批：寫出思患豫防之意，鑿鑿可行，佳士也。
考試官訓導桑批：詞整意足，書卷之最者。
考試官教授林批：發明傅說告君之意殆盡。

惟能防患於未然，斯能免患於將然。夫思患豫
translation_en:
…then the Way of humanity is fully realized. We may thus see that Heaven, through ease, directs beginnings above, while I, through ease, establish my position in the midst and participate with Heaven above; Earth, through simplicity, brings things to completion below, while I, through simplicity, establish my position in the midst and participate with Earth below. This is the supreme achievement of embodying the Way, the consummate work of the sage. What more could be added at this point? Ah! In the Changes, ease and simplicity express principle in its utmost perfection. Qian and Kun generate the myriad things, and the sage participates with the two primal powers: all rests on this alone. Yet the superficial scholars of later ages make their minds devious and obstructed and their conduct vexatious and confused. They already run counter to principle; how much less can they aspire to worthiness, to sagehood, or to Heaven! Only after understanding this can one discuss the Changes.

Book of Documents
“Only by attending to every affair can there be preparedness; with preparedness, there is no calamity.”
Sun Yue 孫鑰

Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “This precisely conveys the meaning of taking Heaven’s keen hearing and clear vision as one’s model.”

Associate Examiner Lu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The argument is built upon the expressions ‘before it happens’ and ‘when it is about to happen’; the conception is fresh. Fu Yue’s intent in admonishing his ruler stands vividly before our eyes. An outstanding selection from this examining section; from this small sample I venture a prediction of his future [?].”

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “It expresses the intention of considering possible calamities and preventing them beforehand, in definite and practicable terms. An excellent scholar.”

Examiner Sang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The language is well ordered and the meaning fully expressed: the best of the Book of Documents scripts.”

Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: “It elucidates almost completely Fu Yue’s intent in admonishing his ruler.”

Only by preventing calamity before it happens can one escape it when it is about to happen. Now, to consider possible calamities and take advance…

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
防君道所當盡也傅說得不以為高宗告哉謂
夫天下之事理亂安危相為倚伏苟不防於未
然而徒悔於將然豈憲天聰明者邪彼事有大
小也知理焉亂所伏必展轉於心思使豫有一
定之謀于以為大於其小則事其事而事乃有
備矣事既有備雖一旦沓至於倉卒之間吾應
之之具已利奚患哉事有難易也知安焉危所
倚必經畫於方寸俾先有審處之術于以圖難
於其易則事其事而事乃有備矣事既有備雖
===
一旦紛擾於急遽之時吾酬之之策無窮奚患
哉如事莫大乎兵不事兵事如外侮何脩車馬
備器械以事乎兵事則兵有其備而外侮不能
為之憂矣事莫難於農不事農事如水旱何簡
稼器脩稼政以事乎農事則農有其備而水旱
不能為之害矣事事有備無患者如此則常理
而不亂安而不危矣憲天聰明之道豈外是哉
嗟夫防患於未然者易為力防患於將然者難
為功故傅說告高宗憲天聰明而必以是為言
punctuated: 防，君道所當盡也。傅說得不以為高宗告哉？謂夫天下之事，理亂安危，相為倚伏。苟不防於未然而徒悔於將然，豈憲天聰明者邪？彼事有大小也，知理焉亂所伏，必展轉於心思，使豫有一定之謀，于以為大於其小，則事其事而事乃有備矣。事既有備，雖一旦沓至於倉卒之間，吾應之之具已利，奚患哉？事有難易也，知安焉危所倚，必經畫於方寸，俾先有審處之術，于以圖難於其易，則事其事而事乃有備矣。事既有備，雖一旦紛擾於急遽之時，吾酬之之策無窮，奚患哉？如事莫大乎兵，不事兵事，如外侮何？脩車馬，備器械，以事乎兵事，則兵有其備，而外侮不能為之憂矣。事莫難於農，不事農事，如水旱何？簡稼器，脩稼政，以事乎農事，則農有其備，而水旱不能為之害矣。事事有備無患者如此，則常理而不亂，安而不危矣。憲天聰明之道，豈外是哉？嗟夫！防患於未然者易為力，防患於將然者難為功。故傅說告高宗憲天聰明，而必以是為言，
translation_en: …prevention is a duty that the ruler must fully discharge. Could Fu Yue fail to offer this counsel to Gaozong? In the affairs of the world, order and disorder, security and danger depend upon one another and lie concealed within one another. If one fails to take precautions before trouble arises and merely regrets it when it is about to arise, can this be called emulating Heaven’s keenness of hearing and sight? Affairs may be great or small. Knowing that disorder lurks within order, one must turn matters over repeatedly in one’s mind, establishing a definite plan beforehand. By thus dealing with great matters while they are still small, one attends to each affair and makes preparations for it. Once preparations are in place, even if affairs suddenly descend upon one in rapid succession, the means of responding are already ready for use. What need is there to worry? Affairs may be difficult or easy. Knowing that danger rests upon security, one must plan within one’s heart, first devising a method for handling matters judiciously. By thus planning for difficulties while matters are still easy, one attends to each affair and makes preparations for it. Once preparations are in place, even if affairs suddenly become tumultuous in a moment of urgency, one’s strategies for responding are inexhaustible. What need is there to worry? For example, no affairs are greater than military affairs. If one neglects military affairs, how can one deal with foreign aggression? By putting chariots and horses in good condition and preparing weapons and equipment, one attends to military affairs. The military is then prepared, and foreign aggression cannot become a source of anxiety. No affairs are more difficult than agriculture. If one neglects agricultural affairs, how can one deal with floods and droughts? By inspecting agricultural implements and putting agricultural administration in order, one attends to agricultural affairs. Agriculture is then prepared, and floods and droughts cannot cause harm. If every affair is thus prepared for and free from trouble, there will always be order without disorder and security without danger. Could the way of emulating Heaven’s keenness of hearing and sight lie outside this? Alas! When one guards against trouble before it arises, one’s efforts are readily effective; when one guards against it only as it is about to arise, success is difficult. Thus, when Fu Yue counseled Gaozong to emulate Heaven’s keenness of hearing and sight, he necessarily spoke of this…

text:
豈非惓惓愛君之深意乎在易之既濟曰君子
思患豫防在詩之鴟鴞曰迨天之未陰雨徹彼
桑土綢繆牖戶即此意也有天下者鑒諸
冢宰掌邦治統百官均四海
孫鑰

同考試官訓導陸批說冢宰掌邦治處甚佳
同考試官教諭李批周官一篇文有典則氣出雄渾是用錄出
===
考試官訓導桑批渾然不費斧鑿其老匠之善雕者
考試官教授林批理明詞暢
賢王正天官以掌邦治其職為甚重焉盖百官
四海皆治道之所在也統之均之天官之職其
重矣哉昔成王董正治官而訓迪其職如此夫
冢宰者天官卿治官之長列六卿而尊於五卿
分一職而兼乎衆職盖天子之相也所掌者豈
非邦治乎邦治者何統百官均四海是已是故
司徒宗伯各有其屬司馬司寇司空亦各有其
punctuated:
豈非惓惓愛君之深意乎？在《易》之《既濟》曰：「君子思患豫防。」在《詩》之《鴟鴞》曰：「迨天之未陰雨，徹彼桑土，綢繆牖戶。」即此意也。有天下者鑒諸！

冢宰掌邦治，統百官，均四海。
孫鑰

In the Book of Changes, the hexagram Already Completed says: “The gentleman considers potential troubles and guards against them beforehand.” In the Book of Odes, “The Owl” says: “Before the sky grows cloudy and rain falls, I strip those mulberry roots and bind up my nest’s windows and doors.” These express this very idea. Let those who possess all under Heaven take heed!

“The Grand Steward directs the governance of the realm, commands the hundred officials, and brings equitable order to all within the Four Seas.”
By Sun Yue 孫鑰.

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
屬敎化禮樂之殊刑政邦土之異冢宰則管攝
使歸于一焉然非官官而控制之自百而歸六
自六而歸一所操者至簡也東西相距海宇如
彼其廣南北相去地里如彼其遠風俗之異宜
人民之殊好冢宰則調劑使得其平焉然非人
人而稱量之大與之爲大小與之爲小所居者
至易也百官異職而能統之則倫要綱紀咸得
其序矣四海異宜而能均之則遠近多寡咸得
其正矣冢宰掌邦治而職任之重有如此成王
===
得不董正而訓迪哉抑嘗考之周家之冢宰即
唐虞之百揆統百官均四海即亮采惠疇也冢
宰之職所係甚重故三代之君知其重而不輕
以授人而其臣亦知其所重而不敢少曠其官
是以當時庶政惟和萬國咸寧者有由然矣後
世有志於三代之治者尚鑒茲哉
詩
之子于苗選徒囂囂建旟設旄搏獸于敖駕
彼四牡四牡奕奕赤芾金舄會同有繹
punctuated:
屬，敎化禮樂之殊，刑政邦土之異，冢宰則管攝，使歸于一焉。然非官官而控制之，自百而歸六，自六而歸一，所操者至簡也。東西相距，海宇如彼其廣；南北相去，地里如彼其遠。風俗之異宜，人民之殊好，冢宰則調劑，使得其平焉。然非人人而稱量之，大與之爲大，小與之爲小，所居者至易也。百官異職而能統之，則倫要綱紀咸得其序矣；四海異宜而能均之，則遠近多寡咸得其正矣。冢宰掌邦治，而職任之重有如此，成王得不董正而訓迪哉？抑嘗考之，周家之冢宰，即唐虞之百揆；統百官、均四海，即亮采惠疇也。冢宰之職所係甚重，故三代之君知其重而不輕以授人，而其臣亦知其所重而不敢少曠其官。是以當時庶政惟和，萬國咸寧者，有由然矣。後世有志於三代之治者，尚鑒茲哉！

詩

之子于苗，選徒囂囂。建旟設旄，搏獸于敖。駕彼四牡，四牡奕奕。赤芾金舄，會同有繹。
translation_en:
…their subordinate officials. Though education, ritual, and music differ, and punishments, administration, and territorial affairs are distinct, the Grand Steward oversees them and brings them into unity. Yet he does not control each official individually: the hundred offices are brought under the six ministers, and the six under one. What he holds in his hands is thus exceedingly simple. From east to west, the realm is so vast; from north to south, the distances are so great. Where customs call for different arrangements and the people have different preferences, the Grand Steward makes adjustments so that all attain a proper balance. Yet he does not weigh each person individually: he treats the great according to their magnitude and the small according to theirs. His position is thus one of the utmost ease. If he can unite the hundred officials despite their different duties, the essential relationships and governing framework will all find their proper order. If he can bring balance to all within the Four Seas despite their differing needs, the distant and the near, the numerous and the few, will all receive their due. The Grand Steward directs the government of the realm, and his responsibilities are weighty indeed. How could King Cheng fail to supervise and rectify his conduct, and instruct and guide him?

Moreover, examining the matter, we find that the Grand Steward of the Zhou was equivalent to the Chief Minister of the Tang and Yu eras. Uniting the hundred officials and bringing balance to the Four Seas meant assisting in public affairs and harmonizing their various categories. The office of Grand Steward had matters of immense importance entrusted to it. Thus the rulers of the Three Dynasties understood its importance and did not confer it lightly; their ministers likewise understood the weight of their responsibilities and dared not neglect their office even slightly. There was therefore good reason why all branches of government were harmonious and the myriad states were at peace in those days. May those in later ages who aspire to the governance of the Three Dynasties take this as their lesson!

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:

黃旣駕兩驂不猗不失其馳舍矢如破蕭
蕭馬鳴悠悠旆旌徒御不驚大庖不盈之
子于征有聞無聲允矣君子展也大成
楊子器
同考試官教諭程批〔形容宣王朝會田獵之盛能噓繁辭而留眞液可嘉可嘉〕
考試官訓導蔡批〔束繁就簡辭理俱到僅見此篇〕
考試官教授林批〔題長而善於該括可取〕
===

而深美之也蓋會同而田獵事有終始也賢君
舉田獵於會同之餘詩人安得不歷敘而深美
之哉思昔宣王興周業於中衰復朝會之故典
鸞輿始至於東都有司先爲之戒具選徒囂囂
衆且肅矣建旐設旄序且整矣待畢會同之禮
將以搏獸于敖斯時也諸侯四牡之是駕望洛
水以朝宗者何連絡布散歟赤芾金舃之是服
覲天顏于咫尺者何陳列聨屬歟會同旣畢田
punctuated:
拾旣佽，弓矢旣調，射夫旣同，助我舉柴。四黃旣駕，兩驂不猗，不失其馳，舍矢如破。蕭蕭馬鳴，悠悠旆旌，徒御不驚，大庖不盈。之子于征，有聞無聲。允矣君子，展也大成。

translation_en:
…The armguards are fitted, the bows and arrows adjusted. The archers have assembled to help us raise the piled game. Four yellow horses are harnessed; the two outer horses do not swerve. They keep to their course, and the arrows fly as though piercing through. The horses neigh, the banners stream afar. Foot soldiers and charioteers remain composed; the great kitchen is not overfilled. This lord goes forth: his renown is heard, but there is no clamor. Trustworthy indeed is the noble lord; truly great is his achievement.
Yang Ziqi.
Comment by Associate Examiner Cheng, Instructor: 〔In depicting the splendor of King Xuan’s court assemblies and hunts, he can winnow away elaborate wording while retaining the true essence. Admirable, admirable!〕
Comment by Examiner Cai, Assistant Instructor: 〔He reduces complexity to simplicity, fully realizing both expression and principle. This is the only essay of its kind I have seen.〕
Comment by Examiner Lin, Professor: 〔Though the set passage is long, he is adept at encompassing it all. Worth selecting.〕
The poet recounts in detail how a worthy ruler conducted a hunt in conjunction with an assembly of the feudal lords; he necessarily narrates the whole course of events, from beginning to end, and praises it profoundly. For an assembly followed by a hunt is an affair with a beginning and an end. When a worthy ruler holds a hunt after the assembly, how could the poet fail to recount it in detail and praise it profoundly? Consider King Xuan of old: he revived the enterprise of Zhou during its decline and restored the ancient institutions of court assemblies. As his phoenix-belled carriage first arrived at the eastern capital, the responsible officials had already made preparations. “The chosen foot soldiers are numerous”: their multitude was also disciplined. “The banners are raised and the yak-tail standards set up”: their ranks were also orderly. Once the ceremonies of the assembly were completed, they would hunt the beasts at Ao. title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
獵攸舉决拾則在指在臂之相比弓矢則强弱
輕重之相得諸侯之人咸於此乎協同所獲之
禽使於此乎助舉心之齊也爲何如駕四馬以
純黃正兩驂而不猗御能不詭而中馳驅之法
舍矢如破而得巧力之全藝之善也爲何如旣
而耳所聞者蕭蕭馬鳴而已目所覩者悠悠斾
旌而已徒御雖眾安靜不見其驚擾獲禽雖多
君庖不見其充盈此盖終事嚴而頒禽均也夫
始聞師眾之征而不聞其聲此嚴肅也終聞師
===
眾之行而聲無所聞亦此嚴肅也使有始而不
謹其終或有終而不善其始謂之君子大成可
乎今焉自始至終一嚴而無間由終達始一肅
而無殊信矣其君子也誠哉其大成也吁宣王
一朝會田獵間而中興之盛美豈不從可見哉
抑考畋于有洛五子作歌以戒太康矣恒于遊
畋伊尹作訓以戒太甲矣車攻之詩若喜談而
樂道之何邪盖周公相成王營洛邑爲東都以
朝諸侯周室旣衰久廢其禮宣王始有以恢復
punctuated: 獵攸舉，决拾則在指在臂之相比，弓矢則强弱輕重之相得。諸侯之人咸於此乎協同，所獲之禽使於此乎助舉，心之齊也爲何如！駕四馬以純黃，正兩驂而不猗，御能不詭而中馳驅之法，舍矢如破而得巧力之全，藝之善也爲何如！旣而耳所聞者蕭蕭馬鳴而已，目所覩者悠悠斾旌而已。徒御雖眾，安靜不見其驚擾；獲禽雖多，君庖不見其充盈。此盖終事嚴而頒禽均也。夫始聞師眾之征而不聞其聲，此嚴肅也；終聞師眾之行而聲無所聞，亦此嚴肅也。使有始而不謹其終，或有終而不善其始，謂之君子大成可乎？今焉自始至終，一嚴而無間；由終達始，一肅而無殊。信矣其君子也，誠哉其大成也！吁！宣王一朝會田獵間，而中興之盛美豈不從可見哉！抑考畋于有洛，五子作歌以戒太康矣；恒于遊畋，伊尹作訓以戒太甲矣。《車攻》之詩若喜談而樂道之，何邪？盖周公相成王，營洛邑爲東都，以朝諸侯。周室旣衰，久廢其禮，宣王始有以恢復
translation_en:
…the hunt was undertaken. The thumb rings on their fingers and the bracers on their arms were suitably paired, and the bows and arrows were matched in strength and weight. The men of the feudal lords all cooperated here, and they were made to help carry the captured game. How united their hearts were! They harnessed four horses of a uniform yellow and kept the two outer horses aligned, without their veering aside. The charioteers avoided irregular movements and observed the rules of driving; the archers released their arrows with penetrating force, fully combining skill and strength. How excellent their accomplishments were!

Then all that the ear heard was the neighing of horses, and all that the eye beheld was the leisurely movement of banners. Though the foot soldiers and charioteers were numerous, they remained quiet, showing no sign of alarm or disturbance. Though much game was taken, the ruler’s kitchen showed no sign of being filled to overflowing. This was because discipline remained strict through the conclusion of the hunt and the game was distributed equitably. At the outset one heard of the host’s setting forth, yet heard no noise from it: such was its discipline and solemnity. At the end one heard of the host’s movement, yet no sound was heard: this was the same discipline and solemnity. If there were a beginning but no care taken over the conclusion, or a conclusion but no proper beginning, could this be called a gentleman’s consummate accomplishment? Here, from beginning to end, discipline remained uninterrupted; looking back from end to beginning, solemnity remained unchanged. Truly he was a gentleman! Indeed, his accomplishment was consummate!

Ah! In King Xuan’s court assembly and hunt, can we not discern the splendor of his restoration? Yet consider hunting in the region of the Luo: the five sons composed their song to admonish Tai Kang. Against habitual pleasure excursions and hunting, Yi Yin composed instructions to admonish Tai Jia. Why, then, does the poem “Our Chariots Were Stout” (Che gong) seem to delight in speaking of and celebrating this? The Duke of Zhou, while assisting King Cheng, built Luoyi as the eastern capital in which to receive the feudal lords at court. After the house of Zhou declined, these rites had long fallen into disuse. Only with King Xuan were there means to restore…

耕餉之人而洽慰勞之情治世之氣象也甚矣
===
周人夫婦之厚也交相慰勞于耕餉之所不厚
而能若是乎載芟詩人之意謂夫國以農爲本
農以勤爲先東作方興南畝俶載侯主侯伯之
具在而飲食必資諸婦人侯亞侯旅之畢集而
饁餉必責諸内助沾體塗足於載芟載柞之餘
耕非不勞也乃以爲男子當務而不辭惟知來

勞爲之曲盡載筐及筥於徂隰徂畛之際餉非
不煩也乃以爲婦人常職而不憚惟知在田者

之，因田獵而示車馬之盛、紀律之嚴，所以爲中興之勢者在此，其諸異乎尋常之田歟？
思媚其婦，有依其士。

Associate Examiner Cheng, Instructor, comments: “It portrays the affection between husbands and wives as they till the fields and bring food, making it vividly present before our eyes. The conclusion is especially unexpected.”
Examiner Sang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “This piece clearly reveals an atmosphere of peace in the countryside.”

Those who till the fields and those who bring them food share feelings of comfort and solicitude: this is the atmosphere of a well-governed age. How profound was the affection between husbands and wives among the people of Zhou! They comforted and encouraged one another where they tilled and brought food. Without profound affection, could they have been like this? The intention of the poet of ‘They Clear Away the Grass’ (Zai shan) was to say that agriculture is the foundation of the state, and diligence comes first in agriculture. Spring cultivation is just beginning; work commences in the southern fields. Masters and eldest sons are all present, but for food and drink they must rely on the women. Younger sons and the assembled workers have all gathered, but the delivery of meals must fall to their wives, their helpers within the household.
With bodies drenched and feet muddied after clearing grass and trees, the men certainly find plowing laborious. Yet they regard it as a man's proper duty and do not shirk it. They think only of those bringing their meals: women of delicate constitution from the inner chambers, who cannot readily endure the journey. With gentleness and affection, they offer them comfort and encouragement in every considerate way. Carrying square and round baskets as they make their way to the lowlands and the field paths, the women certainly find bringing food burdensome. Yet they regard it as a woman's regular duty and do not dread it. They think only of those working in the fields…

text:
風雨侵凌飢渴有所不免以恩以愛而慰勞焉
之周至如兄如弟藹然其親厚所謂黽勉同心
者有矣爰笑爰語驩然其和樂所謂琴瑟靜好
者有矣噫以耕餉之人而洽慰勞之情如此使
非治隆於上俗美於下安能有此氣象哉宜乎
詩人有以頌之也抑攷之中谷有蕹之詩曰嘅
其嘆矣遇人之艱難矣婦見棄於其夫而夫道
薄矣北門之詩曰我入自外室人交徧謫我夫
見困於其婦而婦道薄矣載芟夫婦乃能均致
===
其厚雖野處無異於室家之常其得諸人文之
化豈淺淺哉先儒有曰世治則室家相保者上
之所養也信夫
春秋

風雨侵凌，飢渴有所不免，以恩以愛而慰勞焉之周至。如兄如弟，藹然其親厚，所謂黽勉同心者有矣；爰笑爰語，驩然其和樂，所謂琴瑟靜好者有矣。噫！以耕餉之人而洽慰勞之情如此，使非治隆於上、俗美於下，安能有此氣象哉？宜乎詩人有以頌之也。抑攷之《中谷有蕹》之詩曰：「嘅其嘆矣，遇人之艱難矣。」婦見棄於其夫，而夫道薄矣。《北門》之詩曰：「我入自外，室人交徧謫我。」夫見困於其婦，而婦道薄矣。《載芟》夫婦乃能均致其厚，雖野處，無異於室家之常，其得諸人文之化豈淺淺哉？先儒有曰：「世治則室家相保者，上之所養也。」信夫！

…were battered by wind and rain and could not escape hunger and thirst; with kindness and affection, they offered comfort and encouragement with the utmost care [?]. Like elder and younger brothers, they were warmly affectionate: here was what is called “striving diligently with one heart.” Laughing and talking together, they were joyfully harmonious: here was what is called “the quiet concord of zithers.” Ah! That those who ploughed and those who brought them food should express such mutual concern through comfort and encouragement—without flourishing government above and fine customs below, how could such a scene have existed? It was fitting that the poet should celebrate it.
Yet consider the poem “In the Valley There Is Water Spinach” (Zhong gu you weng) [?], which says: “Deep are her sighs; hard indeed is her lot in the man she has met.” The wife is abandoned by her husband: the husband's fulfillment of his proper role has grown deficient. The poem “North Gate” says: “When I come in from outside, the people of my household join in reproaching me.” The husband is harassed by his wife: the wife's fulfillment of her proper role has grown deficient. The husbands and wives in “They Clear Away the Grass” (Zai shan), however, are equally able to show deep affection. Though out in the fields, they are no different from their usual selves at home. Could the benefit they received from the transforming influence of civilized culture have been slight? An earlier Confucian scholar said: “When the age is well governed, husbands and wives sustain one another because those above have nurtured them.” How true!

且夫君臣人道大倫班位上下猶天尊地卑不

桓控大國扶小國特會首止以定之而王世子
在焉然世子儲貳也下會諸侯則陵諸侯人臣
也上與王世子會則抗春秋特書及以會者若
曰世子在是諸侯往會示不可得而抗也未幾

Wu Yun

Associate Examiner Zheng, School Instructor, comments: “This essay alone grasps the meaning of the commentary and has prose sufficient to bring it out.”
Examiner Sang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Rigorous in expression and correct in meaning: a masterpiece.”
Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “It grasps the intent of honoring the ruler and restraining his subjects.”

When recording the hegemon’s meetings and covenants with the ruler or ministers of the royal house, the Spring and Autumn Annals invariably employs exacting language to rectify the distinctions of status and duty between superior and inferior. For the Spring and Autumn Annals was composed to articulate these distinctions. How, then, could it fail to convey its meaning profoundly in its accounts of Duke Huan of Qi’s meetings and covenants at Shouzhi, Tao, and Kuiqiu? The relationship between ruler and subject is a cardinal bond of human society. Their higher and lower stations are like Heaven’s exaltation and Earth’s lowliness: they must not be confounded. As the world entered the Spring and Autumn period, this principle became obscured. When the Sage drew upon historical records to compile the Classic, how indeed did he enforce these distinctions of status and duty?

Consider King Hui’s excessive fondness, which left his son Zheng’s position imperiled and uncertain. Duke Huan of Qi directed the great states and supported the small, convening a special meeting at Shouzhi to settle the matter; the royal heir apparent was present. Yet the heir apparent was the successor to the throne: to descend to meet the feudal lords would violate the hierarchy [?]. The feudal lords were subjects: to rise to meet the royal heir apparent would be to claim parity with him. Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals deliberately uses “and” before “met,” as if to say: “The heir apparent was here, and the feudal lords went to meet him.” This shows that they could not claim parity with him.

Before long, the royal house announced that it was in distress, and a royal representative duly arrived. Duke Huan of Qi assembled the feudal lords and bound friendly states by agreement, renewing the covenant at Tao to bring security to the royal house; the royal representative participated. Yet the royal representative was an officer of the lowest rank. To list him after the feudal lords would slight the king’s command; to distinguish his participation from the feudal lords’ meeting would treat him as equal to the heir apparent. title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
惟重示不可得而輕也已而天下之大本已定
大勢已安文武之胙頒賜於伯舅宰孔將命下
會于葵丘夫孔以冢宰兼三公其職任重矣春
秋曷為亦例常詞而不殊會之邪誠以天無二
日尊無二上宰孔之爵貴則貴矣上視世子乃
儲君也尊則尊矣下視王人均人臣也人臣則
有進退之節出入均勞之義苟待以殊詞則尊
卑不分君臣之義何有哉故會葵丘之書宰周
公祗與盟洮王人同序於諸侯之上而不與首
===
止王世子殊會同書則天尊地卑而其分定典
敘禮秩而其義明上下辨而班位正矣聖人尊
君抑臣之旨何其嚴歟雖然聖人尊君大法豈
惟是哉他如書王正月以大一統書從王伐鄭
以正分義晉文召王而書狩劉成伐秦而不書
從所以扶天常立人紀無往而不寓焉萬世之
下君君而臣臣父父而子子誰之功歟宰我謂
夫子賢於堯舜信不誣矣
晉士鞅宋樂祁犁衛北宮喜曹人邾人滕人
punctuated:
惟重，示不可得而輕也。已而天下之大本已定，大勢已安，文武之胙頒賜於伯舅，宰孔將命，下會于葵丘。夫孔以冢宰兼三公，其職任重矣，春秋曷為亦例常詞而不殊會之邪？誠以天無二日，尊無二上。宰孔之爵，貴則貴矣，上視世子，乃儲君也；尊則尊矣，下視王人，均人臣也。人臣則有進退之節、出入均勞之義，苟待以殊詞，則尊卑不分，君臣之義何有哉？故會葵丘之書宰周公，祗與盟洮王人同序於諸侯之上，而不與首止王世子殊會同書，則天尊地卑而其分定，典敘禮秩而其義明，上下辨而班位正矣。聖人尊君抑臣之旨，何其嚴歟！雖然，聖人尊君大法，豈惟是哉？他如書王正月以大一統，書從王伐鄭以正分義，晉文召王而書狩，劉成伐秦而不書從，所以扶天常、立人紀，無往而不寓焉。萬世之下，君君而臣臣，父父而子子，誰之功歟？宰我謂夫子賢於堯舜，信不誣矣。
晉士鞅、宋樂祁犁、衛北宮喜、曹人、邾人、滕人
translation_en:
…is nevertheless weighty, showing that it must not be slighted. Thereafter, once the great foundation of All under Heaven was established and its overall situation secure, sacrificial meat offered to Kings Wen and Wu was bestowed upon the ruler addressed as “senior maternal uncle.” Zai Kong bore the royal command and descended to attend the meeting at Kuiqiu. Kong held the office of Grand Steward concurrently with a position among the Three Dukes: his responsibilities were weighty indeed. Why, then, did the Spring and Autumn Annals again employ its usual wording, without distinguishing his participation in the meeting?
This was truly because Heaven has no two suns, and there cannot be two supreme authorities. Noble though Zai Kong’s rank was, when one looks above him to the heir apparent, the latter was the future sovereign. Honored though Zai Kong was, when one looks below him to the king’s representative, both were equally subjects. Subjects must observe the proper rules of advancing and withdrawing and the obligation to share the labors of service both outside and within the court. If he were accorded distinctive wording, superior and inferior would cease to be distinguished. What would then remain of the proper relationship between ruler and subject? Thus, in recording the meeting at Kuiqiu, the Annals merely placed the Duke of Zhou, the Grand Steward, ahead of the feudal lords, just as it placed the king’s representative at the covenant at Tao. It did not record his participation with the distinctive wording used for the royal heir apparent at Shouzhi. In this way, Heaven is exalted and Earth lowly, and their respective positions are fixed; established norms are duly ordered and ritual ranks arranged, and their meaning becomes clear. Superiors and inferiors are distinguished, and precedence and position are rectified. How rigorous was the sage’s purpose in honoring the ruler and restraining his subjects!
Yet was this the only expression of the sage’s great principle of honoring the ruler? Other examples include writing “the king’s first month” to exalt unified rule, and writing “followed the king in attacking Zheng” to rectify the duties of rank. When Duke Wen of Jin summoned the king, the Annals wrote that the king went hunting; when Duke Cheng of Liu attacked Qin, it did not write “followed.” In supporting Heaven’s constant order and establishing the guiding principles of human relations, there is nowhere that this purpose is absent. Through ten thousand generations, rulers act as rulers, subjects as subjects, fathers as fathers, and sons as sons: whose achievement is this? Zai Wo said that the Master surpassed Yao and Shun in worth. Truly, this was no false claim.

會于扈。昭公二十七年。
胡儀

考試官訓導桑批：嚴整。

春秋列序大夫於會者，不以伯臣之貪利而廢其勤義也。觀諸會扈之書法，厥旨深矣。慨自子朝搆禍，周室靡寧；意如稔惡，魯昭播遷。維時晉頃主伯，范鞅當國，乃合列國之大夫，同講于扈之好會，于以嚴成周之令，于以倡納公之謀。曰宋曰衛，旣率先固請；曰曹曰邾，亦俛首相從。使鞅於圖周之餘，而伸恤魯之義，則一舉而兩善并矣。夫何季孫之貨一入，納公之謀遂寢，廢天討不行，辭小國以歸。然則是舉也，始為義動，若可取矣；終以利沮，罪孰甚焉？春秋宜有貶詞以彰不職，而諸國皆序，意安在邪？蓋利於納公者，宋衛之大夫也；受賂而不欲納公者，獨范鞅主之耳。又况成周之令行乎？苟或略之，則范鞅受
