Hu Yi

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, School Director: This composition explains the passage listing the great officers clearly and incisively; it merits praise.
Comment by Examiner Sang, Assistant Instructor: Rigorous and orderly.
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: The writing is mature and vigorous.

The Spring and Autumn Annals lists the great officers attending the meeting individually because it does not allow a hegemon’s minister’s greed for gain to efface their efforts in the cause of righteousness. Looking at how it records the meeting at Hu, we find a profound purpose. Alas, since Zichao fomented disorder, the royal house of Zhou had known no peace; as Yiru’s wickedness grew, Duke Zhao of Lu was driven into exile. At that time, Duke Qing of Jin held the hegemony, and Fan Yang directed the state’s affairs. He assembled the great officers of the various states for a friendly meeting at Hu, to give force to the orders concerning Chengzhou and promote a plan to restore the duke. The representatives of Song and Wei took the lead in pressing this request, while those of Cao and Zhu also bowed their heads in assent. Had Yang, besides making provision for Zhou, fulfilled the righteous duty of aiding Lu, a single undertaking would have accomplished two good ends. Yet once Jisun’s gifts came in, the plan to restore the duke was shelved. Heaven’s punitive justice was abandoned and left unexecuted; he took leave of the smaller states and returned home. Thus this undertaking began as an act prompted by righteousness and seemed commendable, but in the end was thwarted by gain. What offense could be greater? The Spring and Autumn Annals ought to have used condemnatory wording to expose this failure of duty. Yet it lists all the states individually: what is the intention here?

Those who favored restoring the duke were the great officers of Song and Wei; it was Fan Yang alone who took bribes and directed the opposition to restoring him. Moreover, were not the orders concerning Chengzhou carried out? If the account were to omit them, then Fan Yang’s receiving …

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
賂可罪也宋衛之臣何辜棄魯可責也致周之
戍奚尤聖人公是非於筆削之間故會扈之役
列序諸國之大夫者不欲以一人累眾人一惡
掩他善也其取舎之大情輕重之權衡豈不因
是而具見也哉大抵聖人立法謹嚴宅心忠恕
惡者或少貸而與人為善之心常汲汲也彼若
秦伯悔過則取之楚子慕義則進之厥憗序謀
蔡之大夫伐邾釋宋公之取邑凡此類不一而
足其善善長惡惡短之意槩可見矣故曰聖人
===
之心天地之心也
禮記
父子篤兄弟睦夫婦和家之肥也大臣法小
臣廉官職相序君臣相正國之肥也天子
以德為車以樂為御諸侯以禮相與大夫
以法相序士以信相考百姓以睦相守天
下之肥也是謂大順
毛實
同考試官訓導李批〔本傳註而絇之以辭必留心經學者〕
punctuated:
賂可罪也，宋衛之臣何辜？棄魯可責也，致周之戍奚尤？聖人公是非於筆削之間，故會扈之役，列序諸國之大夫者，不欲以一人累眾人、一惡掩他善也。其取舎之大情、輕重之權衡，豈不因是而具見也哉？大抵聖人立法謹嚴，宅心忠恕，惡者或少貸，而與人為善之心常汲汲也。彼若秦伯悔過則取之，楚子慕義則進之，厥憗序謀蔡之大夫，伐邾釋宋公之取邑，凡此類不一而足，其善善長、惡惡短之意槩可見矣。故曰：「聖人之心，天地之心也。」
禮記
父子篤，兄弟睦，夫婦和，家之肥也。大臣法，小臣廉，官職相序，君臣相正，國之肥也。天子以德為車，以樂為御，諸侯以禮相與，大夫以法相序，士以信相考，百姓以睦相守，天下之肥也。是謂大順。
毛實
同考試官訓導李批〔本傳註而絇之以辭，必留心經學者。〕
translation_en:
…accepting bribes deserves condemnation, but what fault had the ministers of Song and Wei committed? Abandoning Lu deserves reproach, but what blame attaches to assembling troops to garrison Zhou? The Sage impartially judged right and wrong through his decisions about what to write and what to delete. Thus, in recording the meeting at Hu, he listed the great officers of the various states in order, unwilling to let one person implicate all the others or one evil obscure other good deeds. Does this not fully reveal the broad intent behind his acceptance and rejection, and the balance by which he weighed their relative importance? In general, the Sage was exacting and rigorous in establishing standards, but loyal and considerate at heart. He sometimes showed a little leniency toward wrongdoers, while always eagerly helping others to do good. Thus, when the Earl of Qin repented his faults, he approved him; when the Viscount of Chu admired righteousness, he advanced him. At Jueyin [?], he listed the great officers who deliberated over Cai; in recording the attack on Zhu, he excused the Duke of Song’s seizure of a town. Examples of this kind are numerous. They broadly reveal his intention to extend praise for goodness and limit condemnation of evil. Hence the saying: “The Sage’s heart is the heart of Heaven and Earth.”
Record of Rites
“When fathers and sons are devoted, brothers affectionate, and husbands and wives harmonious, the household flourishes. When high ministers observe proper standards, subordinate ministers are incorruptible, offices have their proper order, and ruler and ministers correct one another, the state flourishes. When the Son of Heaven takes virtue as his carriage and music as his driver; when the regional lords deal with one another through ritual propriety, great officers order their relations according to established standards, servicemen assess one another by trustworthiness, and the common people sustain one another in amity, all under Heaven flourishes. This is called the Great Accord.”
Mao Shi
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor: 〔“He bases his work on the transmitted commentaries and binds them together with his phrasing [?]. He must be someone who applies himself to the study of the Classics.”〕

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官訓導桑批說大順處異人
考試官教授林批傑筆
極成物之效此大順之道也蓋家國天下之肥
則成物之效極矣大順之道何以加於是哉且
聖學教養之事不惟有成己之功而已又有成
物之效焉彼一家之內有父子兄弟夫婦也父
慈子孝而篤天性之恩兄友弟恭而序同氣之
好夫先而婦從陽倡而陰和則一家充盛而無
不足矣豈不猶人身之肥乎一國之中有君臣
===
官職也為大臣者克盡為臣之道為小臣者不
虧所守之節官職相序而秩然貴賤之有等君
臣相正而截然名分之不踰則一國充盛而無
不足矣又豈不猶人身之肥乎以至天下之大
天子則由仁義行而以德為可行之車動無不
和而以樂為行車之御諸侯朝聘以時而以禮
相與也大夫上下相讓而以法相序也為士者
莫不久要不忘而以信相考焉為百姓者莫不
友助扶持而以睦相守焉則天下之充盛又何
punctuated:
考試官訓導桑批：說大順處異人。
考試官教授林批：傑筆。
極成物之效，此大順之道也。蓋家國天下之肥，則成物之效極矣。大順之道，何以加於是哉？且聖學教養之事，不惟有成己之功而已，又有成物之效焉。彼一家之內，有父子兄弟夫婦也。父慈子孝，而篤天性之恩；兄友弟恭，而序同氣之好；夫先而婦從，陽倡而陰和，則一家充盛而無不足矣。豈不猶人身之肥乎？一國之中，有君臣官職也。為大臣者，克盡為臣之道；為小臣者，不虧所守之節；官職相序，而秩然貴賤之有等；君臣相正，而截然名分之不踰，則一國充盛而無不足矣。又豈不猶人身之肥乎？以至天下之大，天子則由仁義行，而以德為可行之車；動無不和，而以樂為行車之御。諸侯朝聘以時，而以禮相與也；大夫上下相讓，而以法相序也；為士者，莫不久要不忘，而以信相考焉；為百姓者，莫不友助扶持，而以睦相守焉。則天下之充盛，又何
translation_en:
Examiner Sang, an Assistant Instructor, comments: “His treatment of Great Harmony stands apart from others.”
Examiner Lin, an Instructor, comments: “Outstanding writing.”
To bring the efficacy of perfecting others to its utmost: this is the Way of Great Harmony. For when the family, the state, and all under Heaven flourish, the efficacy of perfecting others has reached its utmost. How could the Way of Great Harmony go beyond this? Moreover, the teaching and nurturing undertaken in the learning of the sages accomplish not only the perfection of oneself but also the perfection of others. Within a family are fathers and sons, elder and younger brothers, and husbands and wives. Fathers are kind and sons filial, deepening the affection rooted in their natural relationship; elder brothers are loving and younger brothers respectful, giving due order to the affection of those who share the same vital breath; husbands lead and wives follow, yang initiates and yin responds harmoniously. Thus the family thrives and lacks nothing. Is this not like the fullness of a well-nourished human body?
Within a state are rulers, ministers, and official posts. Great ministers fully discharge the duties of a minister; lesser ministers do not compromise the integrity they must uphold. Officials occupy their proper order, with high and low ranks clearly distinguished; ruler and ministers correct one another, strictly observing the bounds of their respective stations and duties. Thus the state thrives and lacks nothing. Is this not also like the fullness of a well-nourished human body?
Extending this to the vast realm of all under Heaven, the Son of Heaven acts through benevolence and righteousness, taking virtue as the carriage in which he travels; all his movements are harmonious, and he takes music as the means of driving that carriage. The feudal lords attend court and exchange missions at the proper times, dealing with one another according to ritual. The great officers, higher and lower alike, defer to one another, ordering their relations according to established rules. Among the gentlemen, none forget longstanding pledges, and they assess one another by their trustworthiness. Among the common people, all offer friendly assistance and mutual support, sustaining one another in concord. How, then, could the flourishing of all under Heaven …

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
異於人身之肥哉夫一家之肥而國有不肥固
未足以爲大順也一國之肥而天下有不肥亦
未足以爲大順也家國天下無一不肥至和周
流而無滯聖學之功極矣謂非大順而何斯道
洋溢而無間成物之效至矣又非大順而何吁
大順之道如此記禮運者推而言之示人之意
何如哉不特此也以至天不愛道地不愛寶人
不愛情諸福之物可致之祥莫不畢至皆順之
至也使無成已之極功何以致是邪故曰先王
===
能脩禮以達義體信以達順此順之實也有志
於大順者宜鑒於斯
若此則周道四達禮樂交通則夫武之遲久
不亦宜乎
潘府
同考試官訓導李 批 武樂遲久之義此作得之
考試官訓導桑 批 得作樂象成之意
考試官教授林 批 文贍理明
惟武功成於遲久故武樂宜於遲久蓋作樂所
punctuated:
異於人身之肥哉？夫一家之肥而國有不肥，固未足以爲大順也；一國之肥而天下有不肥，亦未足以爲大順也。家國天下無一不肥，至和周流而無滯，聖學之功極矣，謂非大順而何？斯道洋溢而無間，成物之效至矣，又非大順而何？吁！大順之道如此，記《禮運》者推而言之，示人之意何如哉？不特此也，以至天不愛道，地不愛寶，人不愛情，諸福之物、可致之祥，莫不畢至，皆順之至也。使無成已之極功，何以致是邪？故曰：「先王能脩禮以達義，體信以達順。」此順之實也。有志於大順者，宜鑒於斯。

「若此，則周道四達，禮樂交通，則夫武之遲久，不亦宜乎？」
潘府
同考試官訓導李批：「武樂遲久之義，此作得之。」
考試官訓導桑批：「得作樂象成之意。」
考試官教授林批：「文贍理明。」

惟武功成於遲久，故武樂宜於遲久。蓋作樂所
translation_en:
…how would this differ from the flourishing of the human body? If a household flourishes while the state does not, this certainly does not yet suffice to constitute Great Accord. If a state flourishes while all under Heaven does not, this likewise does not yet suffice to constitute Great Accord. When households, states, and all under Heaven flourish without exception, supreme harmony circulates everywhere without obstruction, and the achievement of sagely learning reaches its utmost. What could this be called but Great Accord? When this Way overflows everywhere without interruption, the work of bringing things to fulfillment reaches its culmination. What else could this be but Great Accord? Ah! Such is the Way of Great Accord. How profound was the intention to instruct others of the author who recorded the “Evolution of Rites” (Liyun), extending and expounding this principle!

Nor does it stop here. Heaven withholds none of its Way, Earth withholds none of its treasures, and people withhold none of their true feelings. All things that bring blessings and all auspicious signs that can be elicited arrive together: these are all the utmost manifestations of accord. Without the supreme achievement of perfecting oneself, how could this be brought about? Thus it is said: “The former kings could cultivate ritual to attain righteousness, and embody trustworthiness to attain accord.” This is the substance of accord. Those who aspire to Great Accord should take this as their guide.

“If this was so, then the Way of Zhou extended in all four directions, and rites and music circulated everywhere. Was it not fitting, then, that the Wu dance should be slow and prolonged?”

Pan Fu.
Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor, comments: “This composition grasps the meaning of the slowness and prolonged duration of the Wu music.”
Examiner Sang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “It grasps the intention of creating music to represent accomplished deeds.”
Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “The writing is rich and the reasoning clear.”

Precisely because the military achievement took a long time to accomplish, it is fitting that the Wu music should be slow and prolonged. For the purpose of creating music is …

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
以象成功也然大武之舞非象武功之遲久哉
昔孔子因賓牟賈武樂之問而告之至此若曰
武王之樂所以遲而又久者豈無自哉盖以武
王之克殷也封帝王之後舉尊賢之典弛政而
倍祿偃武而脩文祭饗朝覲之禮以漸而舉耕
籍養老之儀以次而行于以一天下之人心于
以新天下之耳目是以向也歸自鎬京雖曰以
崇天子周道猶未四達也今則敷布於天下東
西南北無處而非周道之洋溢焉昔也歸于西
===
土雖曰皇王維辟禮樂尚未交通也今則漸被
於九有上下內外無適而非禮樂之貫徹焉夫
其成功若是之遲其歷時若是之久則大武之
作得不象之哉故其舞之始出於行列不惟已
備戒之遲而又總干山立嶷然不動者所以象
其遲以待天下之化耳舞之已就於部位不惟
先備戒之久而又久立於綴乃始作舞者所以
倣其久以待治功之成耳武樂之遲久豈不宜
哉吁作樂象成聞樂知德反覆孔子之論大武
punctuated: 以象成功也。然大武之舞，非象武功之遲久哉？昔孔子因賓牟賈武樂之問而告之至此，若曰：武王之樂所以遲而又久者，豈無自哉？盖以武王之克殷也，封帝王之後，舉尊賢之典，弛政而倍祿，偃武而脩文。祭饗朝覲之禮，以漸而舉；耕籍養老之儀，以次而行。于以一天下之人心，于以新天下之耳目。是以向也歸自鎬京，雖曰以崇天子，周道猶未四達也；今則敷布於天下，東西南北，無處而非周道之洋溢焉。昔也歸于西土，雖曰皇王維辟，禮樂尚未交通也；今則漸被於九有，上下內外，無適而非禮樂之貫徹焉。夫其成功若是之遲，其歷時若是之久，則大武之作得不象之哉？故其舞之始出於行列，不惟已備戒之遲，而又總干山立，嶷然不動者，所以象其遲以待天下之化耳。舞之已就於部位，不惟先備戒之久，而又久立於綴，乃始作舞者，所以倣其久以待治功之成耳。武樂之遲久，豈不宜哉？吁！作樂象成，聞樂知德，反覆孔子之論大武
translation_en:
…to represent accomplished achievements. Does not the dance of the Great Martial Music (Dawu), then, represent the slowness and long duration of King Wu’s achievements? Long ago, when Confucius responded to Binmou Jia’s question about the Martial Music, his explanation reached this point, as if to say: Could the slowness and long duration of King Wu’s music have been without a reason? After King Wu conquered Yin, he enfeoffed the descendants of earlier emperors and kings and instituted ceremonies for honoring the worthy. He relaxed government exactions and doubled stipends, laid down arms and cultivated civil culture. The rites of sacrifice, feasting, and court audience were introduced gradually; the ceremonies of plowing the royal field and caring for the aged were carried out in sequence. By these means he united the hearts of all under Heaven and renewed what they saw and heard. Thus, earlier, when he returned from Haojing, although it was said that this exalted the Son of Heaven, the Way of Zhou had not yet reached all four quarters. Now it spread throughout the realm: east, west, south, and north, there was nowhere that the Way of Zhou did not abundantly prevail. Earlier, when he returned to the western lands, although it was said that the august king was sovereign, rites and music had not yet circulated everywhere. Now they gradually extended throughout the nine regions: above and below, within and without, there was nowhere that rites and music did not penetrate.

Since his achievements were accomplished so slowly and required so long a time, could the composition of the Great Martial Music fail to represent this? Thus, when the dancers first emerge in their ranks, not only is there already a slow preparatory warning, but they also grasp their shields and stand like mountains, lofty and motionless. This represents his slowness as he awaited the transformation of all under Heaven. Once the dancers have taken their assigned positions, not only has there first been a prolonged preparatory warning, but they also stand for a long time at their marked stations before beginning to dance. This imitates the long time he waited for the work of good government to reach completion. Is not the slowness and long duration of the Martial Music therefore fitting? Ah! Music is composed to represent accomplished achievements; by hearing music, one knows virtue. If one ponders repeatedly Confucius’s discussion of the Great Martial Music…

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之樂則武王之功德亦庶乎其可知矣他日又
謂韶盡美矣又盡善也武盡美矣未盡善也何
哉盖舜之德性之也又以揖讓而有天下武王
之德反之也又以征伐而有天下故其實有不
同如此當合而觀之
論
聖人天道之自然
夏鐶
同考試官訓導李批論聖人天道自然處詞理俱到
必有學之士也
===
同考試官教諭程批此作如布帛菽粟足資世用識
者當自知重
考試官訓導孫批此作如登終南太華而步步皆
踏實地與凌虛厲空者異矣
考試官教授林批文理純正傑作也
天之所以爲天聖人之所以爲聖人者一
自然而然也天之道一至誠也聖人之道
亦一至誠也至誠無息不息則不已此理
punctuated:
之樂，則武王之功德亦庶乎其可知矣。他日又謂：「韶盡美矣，又盡善也；武盡美矣，未盡善也。」何哉？盖舜之德，性之也，又以揖讓而有天下；武王之德，反之也，又以征伐而有天下，故其實有不同如此。當合而觀之。

論
聖人天道之自然
夏鐶

同考試官訓導李批：論聖人天道自然處，詞理俱到，必有學之士也。

同考試官教諭程批：此作如布帛菽粟，足資世用，識者當自知重。

考試官訓導孫批：此作如登終南太華，而步步皆踏實地，與凌虛厲空者異矣。

考試官教授林批：文理純正，傑作也。

天之所以爲天，聖人之所以爲聖人者，一自然而然也。天之道，一至誠也；聖人之道，亦一至誠也。至誠無息，不息則不已，此理
translation_en:
…the music, then King Wu’s achievements and virtue may also become comprehensible. On another occasion, Confucius said: “The Shao music is perfectly beautiful and also perfectly good; the Wu music is perfectly beautiful but not perfectly good.” Why was this? Shun possessed virtue by nature and acquired All under Heaven through deferential yielding; King Wu attained virtue by returning to it through effort and acquired All under Heaven through conquest. Thus their actual circumstances differed in this way. These judgments should be considered together.

Discourse
The Sage and the Spontaneity of the Way of Heaven
By Xia Huan 夏鐶

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor: In discussing the spontaneity of the sage and the Way of Heaven, both the language and the reasoning are fully accomplished. The author must be a man of learning.

Comment by Associate Examiner Cheng, Instructor: This composition is like cloth, silk, beans, and grain: it amply serves the needs of the world. Discerning readers will naturally recognize its worth.

Comment by Examiner Sun, Assistant Instructor: This composition is like ascending Zhongnan and Taihua: every step lands on solid ground. It differs from those that soar into the void and stride through empty air.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Professor: Pure and correct in its writing and reasoning—a masterpiece.

What makes Heaven Heaven, and the sage a sage, is simply that each is spontaneously so. The Way of Heaven is nothing but utmost sincerity; the Way of the sage is likewise nothing but utmost sincerity. Utmost sincerity is without respite; without respite, it never ceases. This principle…

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之自然雖欲已之而有不可得者豈故使
之然哉使天而故不已焉是嘗有時而已
矣果足以爲天乎使聖人而故不已焉是
嘗有時而已矣果足以爲聖人乎古之善
言天者曰於穆不已善言聖人者曰文王
之德之純而釋之者以爲天之不已其命
猶聖人之不已其德是以爲有意而爲之
非所以論聖人天道之自然矣請因子朱
子之論而申之道之在天下真實而無妄
===
故謂之誠誠也者天理之自然也誠極其
至則無息自然而不息也不息則久自然
而久也以其在天者言之高者自高明者
自明和煦者自發舒而肅殺者自摧折皆
實有是理而實有是用故春而夏夏而秋
秋而冬冬而復春流行而不可遏也生而
長長而收收而藏藏而復生聯續而不可
斷也是誰爲張主而綱維之哉一實理之
自然也人者得天之道以生者也聖人者
punctuated: 之自然，雖欲已之而有不可得者，豈故使之然哉？使天而故不已焉，是嘗有時而已矣，果足以爲天乎？使聖人而故不已焉，是嘗有時而已矣，果足以爲聖人乎？古之善言天者曰：「於穆不已。」善言聖人者曰：「文王之德之純。」而釋之者以爲天之不已其命，猶聖人之不已其德。是以爲有意而爲之，非所以論聖人天道之自然矣。請因子朱子之論而申之：道之在天下，真實而無妄，故謂之誠。誠也者，天理之自然也。誠極其至則無息，自然而不息也；不息則久，自然而久也。以其在天者言之，高者自高，明者自明，和煦者自發舒，而肅殺者自摧折，皆實有是理而實有是用。故春而夏，夏而秋，秋而冬，冬而復春，流行而不可遏也；生而長，長而收，收而藏，藏而復生，聯續而不可斷也。是誰爲張主而綱維之哉？一實理之自然也。人者，得天之道以生者也。聖人者，
translation_en:
…the natural operation of principle. Even if one wished to stop it, one could not. How could it be deliberately made so? If Heaven deliberately kept itself from ceasing, this would imply that there had been times when it ceased. Could it truly qualify as Heaven? If the sage deliberately kept himself from ceasing, this would imply that there had been times when he ceased. Could he truly qualify as a sage? Those of antiquity who spoke well of Heaven said, “Ah, profound and unceasing!” Those who spoke well of the sage said, “The purity of King Wen’s virtue.” Those who explained these words held that Heaven’s never ceasing in its mandate was like the sage’s never ceasing in his virtue. To regard this as something done intentionally is no way to discuss the natural operation of the sage’s way and Heaven’s way. Allow me to elaborate upon the discussion of Master Zhu.

The Way throughout the world is real and without falsity; hence it is called sincerity. Sincerity is the natural operation of Heaven’s principle. When sincerity reaches its utmost, it is unceasing: it is naturally unceasing. Being unceasing, it endures: it naturally endures. Speaking of its presence in Heaven, what is high is naturally high, and what is bright is naturally bright; what is mild and warming naturally brings forth and unfolds, while what is stern and killing naturally crushes and breaks. In all these cases, this principle truly exists, and this operation truly takes place. Thus spring passes into summer, summer into autumn, autumn into winter, and winter back into spring: their flowing course cannot be checked. Birth passes into growth, growth into gathering, gathering into storage, and storage back into birth: their continuity cannot be broken. Who presides over this and holds it all together? It is simply the natural operation of real principle. Human beings receive Heaven’s Way and thereby come into life. As for the sage, …

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
全天之道而不雜焉者也仁則仁義則義
仁義之外無增益也禮則禮智則智禮智
之外無矯飾也動靜云為無一事之非道
出入起居無一時之非道聖人豈有心而
為之哉亦一實理之自然也是故為子而
朝于王季孝之實也為夫而睦于后妃禮
之實也雝雝焉而在宫肅肅焉而在廟敬
之實也一舉而伐密再舉而伐崇武之實
也故光于四方顯于西土不以遠而殊不
===
殄厥愠不隕厥聞不以險而變文王之聖
曷嘗有一時之息哉使有一毫之偽焉則
飾於外必歉於内非所以為聖人矣使有
一毫之勉焉則勉於此或忽於彼非所以
為聖人矣不足以為聖人則人而已矣不
足以合乎天矣所謂至誠者固如是乎嗚
呼天一聖人也聖人一天也窺聖人而未
極其至則未免以人而論聖人覩天而未
極其至則未免以物而論天也然聖人天
punctuated: 全天之道而不雜焉者也。仁則仁，義則義，仁義之外無增益也；禮則禮，智則智，禮智之外無矯飾也。動靜云為，無一事之非道；出入起居，無一時之非道。聖人豈有心而為之哉？亦一實理之自然也。是故為子而朝于王季，孝之實也；為夫而睦于后妃，禮之實也；雝雝焉而在宫，肅肅焉而在廟，敬之實也；一舉而伐密，再舉而伐崇，武之實也。故光于四方，顯于西土，不以遠而殊；不殄厥愠，不隕厥聞，不以險而變。文王之聖，曷嘗有一時之息哉？使有一毫之偽焉，則飾於外必歉於内，非所以為聖人矣；使有一毫之勉焉，則勉於此或忽於彼，非所以為聖人矣。不足以為聖人，則人而已矣，不足以合乎天矣。所謂至誠者，固如是乎！嗚呼！天一聖人也，聖人一天也。窺聖人而未極其至，則未免以人而論聖人；覩天而未極其至，則未免以物而論天也。然聖人天
translation_en: …those who fully embody the Way of Heaven without admixture. In benevolence they are benevolent; in righteousness, righteous: nothing is added beyond benevolence and righteousness. In ritual propriety they observe propriety; in wisdom they are wise: beyond propriety and wisdom there is no contrived embellishment. In activity and stillness, speech and action, nothing they do lies outside the Way; in going out and coming in, rising and resting, no moment lies outside the Way. Does the sage act with deliberate intent? This too is simply the spontaneous working of the one true principle. Thus, as a son, paying morning attendance upon Wang Ji was the true expression of filial piety; as a husband, living harmoniously with his consort was the true expression of ritual propriety. Being harmonious within the palace and reverent within the ancestral temple was the true expression of respect. Launching one campaign against Mi and another against Chong was the true expression of martial virtue. Thus his light shone throughout the four quarters, and his virtue was manifest in the western lands, without varying with distance. He did not let his indignation die away or his good name fall, remaining unchanged amid peril. When did King Wen’s sageliness ever cease, even for a moment? Had there been the slightest falseness in him, outward embellishment would necessarily have concealed an inward deficiency, and he would not have been a sage. Had there been the slightest forced effort in him, effort in one matter might have meant neglect in another, and he would not have been a sage. If he fell short of being a sage, he would have been merely an ordinary person, unable to accord with Heaven. Such indeed is what is called utmost sincerity! Alas! Heaven is a sage, and the sage is a Heaven. If one examines the sage without comprehending his ultimate perfection, one inevitably judges the sage in terms of ordinary people; if one observes Heaven without comprehending its ultimate perfection, one inevitably judges Heaven in terms of material things. Yet the sage and Heaven…

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
道之所以爲至者亦非幽深恍惚可望而
不可到也乃在於眞實無妄之間固局卑
近者之所不能知亦騖高遠者之所忽也
故曰中庸不可能也中也誠也其一理之
自然者乎夫人非天也人不能皆聖人也
則當勉以求之勉而至於誠則亦聖人矣
亦天矣此則人道之說與論天道者各有
所指而言若遂以爲天人異域凡聖不同
科則亦非所以論天論聖人矣
孫鑰
===
同考試官訓導張批〔筆力蒼健文采燁然風簷寸晷之下能有此作亦爲難得故不厭其複而錄之〕
同考試官教諭李批〔文有發越理亦不背其究心於論學者歟〕
考試官訓導桑批〔此作如商彞周鼎望之皆知爲古器也〕
考試官教授林批〔有源委有操縱論場中之斐然者〕
論曰天人之理誠其至乎聖人也者人之
punctuated:
道之所以爲至者，亦非幽深恍惚、可望而不可到也，乃在於眞實無妄之間。固局卑近者之所不能知，亦騖高遠者之所忽也。故曰：「中庸不可能也。」中也，誠也，其一理之自然者乎！夫人非天也，人不能皆聖人也，則當勉以求之。勉而至於誠，則亦聖人矣，亦天矣。此則人道之說，與論天道者各有所指而言。若遂以爲天人異域，凡聖不同科，則亦非所以論天、論聖人矣。

孫鑰

同考試官教諭李批〔文有發越，理亦不背，其究心於論學者歟！〕

考試官訓導桑批〔此作如商彞周鼎，望之皆知爲古器也。〕

考試官教授林批〔有源委，有操縱，論場中之斐然者。〕

論曰：天人之理，誠其至乎！聖人也者，人之
translation_en:
…What makes the sage and the Way of Heaven supreme is neither something obscure and elusive nor something that can be gazed upon but never attained. It lies in being genuine and free from falsity. Those confined to the lowly and commonplace cannot understand it, while those pursuing the lofty and remote overlook it. Thus it is said: “The Mean cannot be practiced.” Centrality and sincerity—are they not the spontaneous workings of a single principle? Human beings are not Heaven, and not all can be sages; they must therefore strive to attain this. If through striving they attain sincerity, they too become sages and become one with Heaven. This account of the human Way and the discussion of the Way of Heaven each speak with a distinct referent. But to conclude that Heaven and humanity occupy separate realms, or that ordinary people and sages belong to different categories, would likewise be no proper way to discuss Heaven or the sage.

Sun Yue 孫鑰

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
至天也者物之至誠也者天人之至聖人
之所以爲聖人此誠也天之所以爲天此
誠也聖人天道之誠皆迎之而不見其始
之得遡之而不見其終之窮同一自然而
然者也夫豈可以差殊觀哉聖人天道之
自然請以朱子之言而論之誠立聖人之
本聖人乃誠之郛廓誠爲天之根柢而天
乃誠之形體聖人以誠而爲聖人天道以
誠而爲天道分之則爲二合之則爲一者
===
也以聖人言之知焉生知行焉安行性天
之性德天之德語其仁義仁義無一之不
誠語其禮智禮智無一之不誠鬼神莫知
寂然寧謐之境者誠之源儵忽莫鑿熈然
混沌之區者誠之幹何思何慮誠無爲也
所以循環者無終窮不識不知誠無將也
所以周流者無空闕內焉此誠外焉此誠
內外一誠之闔闢少焉此誠老焉此誠老
少一誠之運用聖人之所以爲聖人非一
punctuated:
至，天也者，物之至；誠也者，天人之至。聖人之所以爲聖人，此誠也；天之所以爲天，此誠也。聖人、天道之誠，皆迎之而不見其始之得，遡之而不見其終之窮，同一自然而然者也。夫豈可以差殊觀哉？聖人、天道之自然，請以朱子之言而論之。誠立聖人之本，聖人乃誠之郛廓；誠爲天之根柢，而天乃誠之形體。聖人以誠而爲聖人，天道以誠而爲天道，分之則爲二，合之則爲一者也。
以聖人言之，知焉生知，行焉安行，性天之性，德天之德。語其仁義，仁義無一之不誠；語其禮智，禮智無一之不誠。鬼神莫知，寂然寧謐之境者，誠之源；儵忽莫鑿，熈然混沌之區者，誠之幹。何思何慮，誠無爲也，所以循環者無終窮；不識不知，誠無將也，所以周流者無空闕。內焉此誠，外焉此誠，內外一誠之闔闢；少焉此誠，老焉此誠，老少一誠之運用。聖人之所以爲聖人，非一
translation_en:
…the pinnacle of humanity; Heaven is the pinnacle of all things. Sincerity is the supreme perfection of Heaven and humanity. What makes the sage a sage is this sincerity; what makes Heaven Heaven is this sincerity. The sincerity of the sage and of the Way of Heaven is such that, approaching it, one cannot discern where its beginning is attained, and tracing it back, one cannot discern where its end is exhausted [?]. Both alike are spontaneously so of themselves. How could they be regarded as different? Allow me to discuss this spontaneity of the sage and the Way of Heaven through the words of Master Zhu. Sincerity establishes the foundation of the sage, and the sage is sincerity’s enclosing wall; sincerity is the root of Heaven, and Heaven is sincerity’s embodied form. Through sincerity the sage is a sage, and through sincerity the Way of Heaven is the Way of Heaven. Considered separately, they are two; considered together, they are one.
Speaking of the sage: his knowledge is knowledge possessed from birth, and his conduct is conduct performed with ease. His nature is Heaven’s nature, and his virtue is Heaven’s virtue. Speak of his benevolence and righteousness: neither is anything but sincere. Speak of his ritual propriety and wisdom: neither is anything but sincere. The still and tranquil realm, unknowable even to ghosts and spirits, is the source of sincerity; the harmonious realm of undifferentiated wholeness, which Shu and Hu do not bore into, is sincerity’s trunk. What thought, what deliberation is there? Sincerity acts without contrivance, and thus its cycles have neither end nor exhaustion. Without recognition or knowledge, sincerity has no anticipation, and thus its circulation leaves no gap or deficiency. Within is this sincerity; without is this sincerity. Inner and outer are the closing and opening of a single sincerity. In youth is this sincerity; in old age is this sincerity. Youth and old age are the workings of a single sincerity. Is not what makes the sage a sage a single…

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
誠之自然邪以天道言之穹然其形蒼然
其色日月星辰布其文風雨霜露宣其化
孰為主宰而凡榮瘁開落千古無不同孰
為綱維而凡飛潛蠢動萬世無或異其體
之運行乎度數所以常運行者誠為之樞
其氣之升降乎上下所以常升降者誠為
之轂冲漠無朕誠無形象也而每顯相於
陟降厥士之時曠蕩無涯誠無範圍也而
恒通靈於監觀四方之際元而亨利而貞
===
貞而復元春而夏秋而冬冬而復春動靜
無端一此誠乎機緘何有於矯揉陰陽無
始一此誠乎橐籥何有於造作天之所以
為天又非一誠之自然邪是則天也聖人
也同一誠之自然也誠者太極之理太極
生天天生聖人太極之道盡於天天之道
盡於聖人舍天無以見太極舍聖人無以
見天道聖人也者其天之分形而太極之
委順乎故欲求太極當觀之天欲求天當
punctuated: 誠之自然邪？以天道言之，穹然其形，蒼然其色，日月星辰布其文，風雨霜露宣其化。孰為主宰，而凡榮瘁開落，千古無不同？孰為綱維，而凡飛潛蠢動，萬世無或異？其體之運行乎度數，所以常運行者，誠為之樞；其氣之升降乎上下，所以常升降者，誠為之轂。冲漠無朕，誠無形象也，而每顯相於陟降厥士之時；曠蕩無涯，誠無範圍也，而恒通靈於監觀四方之際。元而亨，利而貞，貞而復元；春而夏，秋而冬，冬而復春。動靜無端，一此誠乎機緘，何有於矯揉？陰陽無始，一此誠乎橐籥，何有於造作？天之所以為天，又非一誠之自然邪？是則天也，聖人也，同一誠之自然也。誠者，太極之理。太極生天，天生聖人。太極之道盡於天，天之道盡於聖人。舍天無以見太極，舍聖人無以見天道。聖人也者，其天之分形而太極之委順乎？故欲求太極，當觀之天；欲求天，當
translation_en: …the spontaneous working of sincerity alone? Speaking of the Way of Heaven: its form is vaulted, its color azure; the sun, moon, and stars array its patterns, while wind, rain, frost, and dew give expression to its transforming power. Who presides over it, such that flourishing and withering, blossoming and falling, remain consistent through a thousand ages? Who holds it together, such that all creatures flying, swimming beneath the waters, or crawling remain constant through ten thousand generations? Its body moves according to measured cycles; that it moves unceasingly is because sincerity serves as its pivot. Its vital energy rises and falls between above and below; that it rises and falls unceasingly is because sincerity serves as its hub. Empty and still, without a trace, sincerity has no visible form; yet it repeatedly manifests its aid when ascending and descending among its officers [?]. Vast and boundless, sincerity has no confines; yet its spiritual efficacy constantly reaches everywhere as Heaven surveys the four quarters. Origination leads to flourishing, benefit to steadfastness, and steadfastness returns to origination; spring leads to summer, autumn to winter, and winter returns to spring. Movement and stillness have no endpoint: sincerity alone operates their mechanism—what room is there for forced adjustment? Yin and yang have no beginning: sincerity alone operates their bellows—what room is there for contrivance? Is not what makes Heaven Heaven likewise the spontaneous working of sincerity alone? Thus Heaven and the sage share the same spontaneous working of sincerity. Sincerity is the principle of the Supreme Ultimate. The Supreme Ultimate generates Heaven, and Heaven generates the sage. The Way of the Supreme Ultimate finds its full expression in Heaven; the Way of Heaven finds its full expression in the sage. Apart from Heaven, there is no means of perceiving the Supreme Ultimate; apart from the sage, there is no means of perceiving the Way of Heaven. Is the sage, then, Heaven embodied in a distinct form and the Supreme Ultimate following its natural course? Therefore, to seek the Supreme Ultimate, one should contemplate Heaven; to seek Heaven, one should…

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
嘗觀之聖人聖人者在下之天天之誠即
聖人之誠也天者在上之聖人聖人之誠
即天之誠也是以天命之不已與聖德之
不已一皆自然而然者也若謂不已其命
而不已其德則是有意於不已詎足以明
聖人天道之自然哉宜子朱子以是箴呂
氏之失也考之子思作中庸二十六章言
天道引詩言維天之命於穆不已蓋曰天
之所以為天也於乎不顯文王之德之純
===
蓋曰文王之所以為文也純亦不已蓋借
文王以見群聖人皆與天而合德也至朱
子又以是為言合而觀之天道無息聖人
亦無息皆此誠也使吾誠一有間斷則與
天不相似矣其能合天而為一乎方今
聖天子在位至誠之德上配天道下浹四方則
又曠千古而一見者也愚也何幸身逢其
盛
表
punctuated:
嘗觀之聖人。聖人者，在下之天，天之誠即聖人之誠也；天者，在上之聖人，聖人之誠即天之誠也。是以天命之不已與聖德之不已，一皆自然而然者也。若謂不已其命而不已其德，則是有意於不已，詎足以明聖人天道之自然哉？宜子朱子以是箴呂氏之失也。考之子思作《中庸》二十六章，言天道，引《詩》言：「維天之命，於穆不已！」蓋曰天之所以為天也。「於乎不顯，文王之德之純！」蓋曰文王之所以為文也。純亦不已，蓋借文王以見群聖人皆與天而合德也。至朱子，又以是為言。合而觀之，天道無息，聖人亦無息，皆此誠也。使吾誠一有間斷，則與天不相似矣，其能合天而為一乎？方今聖天子在位，至誠之德，上配天道，下浹四方，則又曠千古而一見者也。愚也何幸，身逢其盛！

表
translation_en:
…look to the sage. The sage is Heaven below: Heaven’s sincerity is precisely the sage’s sincerity. Heaven is the sage above: the sage’s sincerity is precisely Heaven’s sincerity. Thus the ceaselessness of Heaven’s mandate and the ceaselessness of the sage’s virtue alike arise entirely of themselves. If one speaks of keeping its mandate unceasing and keeping his virtue unceasing, this implies a deliberate intention to remain unceasing. How could that adequately illuminate the spontaneity of the sage and the Way of Heaven? It was fitting that Master Zhu should use this to correct Master Lü’s error.

Examining chapter twenty-six of the Doctrine of the Mean, composed by Zisi, we find that, in discussing the Way of Heaven, he quotes the Book of Odes: “The mandate of Heaven—how profound and unceasing!” This expresses what makes Heaven Heaven. “Ah, how illustrious was the purity of King Wen’s virtue!” This expresses what made King Wen worthy of the name Wen. Purity, too, is unceasing. King Wen is thus taken as an example to show that all sages accord with Heaven in virtue. Master Zhu likewise spoke in these terms. Considered together, the Way of Heaven never ceases, and the sage likewise never ceases: both are this sincerity. Should our sincerity suffer even a single interruption, we would no longer resemble Heaven. Could we then unite with Heaven and become one?

Now the sagely Son of Heaven occupies the throne. His virtue of utmost sincerity accords above with the Way of Heaven and permeates below the four quarters. Here is something witnessed but once across the vast span of the ages. How fortunate am I, ignorant as I am, to live amid this flourishing age!

Memorials

By Yang Ziqi

translation_en:
…from the lofty pavilion, I sought the source of praise and blame; weighing the various interpretations through specialized scholarship, I took up the means of distinguishing right from wrong. To establish the judgments of a single school, I spent several years. Moreover, these retain principles suited to timely application and may warrant troubling Your Majesty to read them late into the night.
Now, fortunately, I humbly encounter 〇〇〇〇: Your Majesty’s intelligence is Heaven-endowed, and your sagely reverence advances daily. You enforce laws and institutions to rectify the officials, and establish distinctions of status to bring order among the people. Your achievements eclipse Emperor Guangwu’s restoration of the dynasty and surpass King Xuan’s revival of ancient ways. Your Way is manifest in governing the state, and you wish to hear the phoenix in the outskirts of Zhou; your purpose lies in ordering the world, and you cherish the unicorn of the marshes of Lu. Deign to consider this foolish servant’s occasional insight, that it may contribute a little to your understanding of the myriad affairs of government.

…strengthen the defenses of the Central Realm. I humbly wish that the waves of the Hanhai may be clear and that throughout the six directions the seasons may forever proceed in perfect harmony; that the dust of conflict may be swept from Moju [?], and that for ten thousand years the realm may remain secure, like an intact golden vessel. Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to the Sage Emperor, cannot contain his utmost fervor and trembling awe. I respectfully submit the Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals that I have composed, accompanying this memorial, for Your Majesty’s attention.

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
指授成於獨斷編摩集乎眾長揆前古之
著述誠未有盛於我
朝
英宗睿皇帝大明一統志之作也四海風俗備
載不遺天下人物詳書靡漏盖欲人知習
尚之弊而自相變易仰前哲之風而自加
飭勵豈徒誇土地之廣饒人物之繁阜而
已哉試以全浙言之禹貢在古揚州之域
天文屬斗牛女之墟聳峙有湖山之秀麗
===
襟帶有江海之吐吞以言其風俗杭州在
藩省之中而嚴州與之接壤一則人性敏
慧而習俗工巧一則人和物阜民貧而嗇
焉嘉興居藩省之北而湖州與之連封一
則知慕文儒而頗勤稼穡一則儒風始盛
而習俗歸美焉至於俗勤耕織而士知所
學俗悍以寡而耿耿好氣非金華之與衢
州乎君子尚禮而小人勤稼俗重犯法而
篤志好學非處州之與紹興乎其俗不雜
punctuated:
指授成於獨斷，編摩集乎眾長。揆前古之著述，誠未有盛於我朝英宗睿皇帝《大明一統志》之作也。四海風俗，備載不遺；天下人物，詳書靡漏。盖欲人知習尚之弊而自相變易，仰前哲之風而自加飭勵，豈徒誇土地之廣饒、人物之繁阜而已哉？試以全浙言之，《禹貢》在古揚州之域，天文屬斗牛女之墟，聳峙有湖山之秀麗，襟帶有江海之吐吞。
以言其風俗，杭州在藩省之中，而嚴州與之接壤，一則人性敏慧而習俗工巧，一則人和物阜，民貧而嗇焉。嘉興居藩省之北，而湖州與之連封，一則知慕文儒而頗勤稼穡，一則儒風始盛而習俗歸美焉。至於俗勤耕織而士知所學，俗悍以寡而耿耿好氣，非金華之與衢州乎？君子尚禮而小人勤稼，俗重犯法而篤志好學，非處州之與紹興乎？其俗不雜
translation_en:
…Its direction proceeded from the sovereign’s sole judgment, while its compilation brought together the strengths of many. Surveying the writings of antiquity, truly none has surpassed the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Great Ming (Da Ming yitong zhi), produced under Emperor Yingzong Rui of our dynasty. The customs within the Four Seas are fully recorded, with nothing omitted; the notable people throughout the realm are described in detail, with none overlooked. The intention was surely that people should recognize the faults in their customary practices and help one another change them, and admire the example of earlier worthies and further discipline and encourage themselves. Could it merely have been to boast of the breadth and richness of the territory and the abundance of its people and talent?
Take Zhejiang as a whole. According to the Tribute of Yu (Yu gong), it lies within the territory of ancient Yangzhou; in celestial correspondence, it belongs to the lodges Dipper, Ox, and Girl. Its lofty heights display the beauty of lakes and mountains, while rivers and seas, receiving and discharging their waters, enfold it like collars and belts.
As for its customs, Hangzhou lies at the center of the province, and Yanzhou adjoins it. In the former, the people are quick-witted and their customary pursuits show ingenuity and skill; in the latter, the people live harmoniously and goods are plentiful, though the common people are poor and frugal. Jiaxing lies in the north of the province, and Huzhou shares its boundary. In the former, people admire literary and Confucian learning and are quite diligent in farming; in the latter, Confucian influence has begun to flourish and customs tend toward goodness. As for a tradition of diligence in plowing and weaving, with scholars knowing what they should study, and customs that are fierce and sparse [?], with people resolute and fond of asserting their spirit—are these not Jinhua and Quzhou? Where gentlemen esteem ritual propriety and commoners diligently cultivate the land, and where people regard breaking the law as a serious matter and are firmly devoted to learning—are these not Chuzhou and Shaoxing? Its customs are unmixed…

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而其人易治衣冠文物甲於東南者寧波
也其人樸靜而其俗儉約閭閻之中興行
禮遜者台州也至於爭訟少而紡績勤器
用備而秔稻足又非温州之所習尚者乎
以言人物陸知命之侃然正色百僚敬憚
王縉之啓沃君心知無不言則出於嚴杭
者也陸贄之論諫切直一本仁義倪思之
論疏剴切悚動人主則生於嘉湖者也金
之與衢則有宗澤之起兵勤王志在興復
===
□□之為政簡靜卒謚清獻者焉處之與
紹則有葉夢得之博學能文尤邃經術嚴
光之少有高名不屈仕進者焉他如陳禾
之引落帝衣不惜碎首非寧波所産乎謝
申甫之愛惜名器扶持正學非台州所産
乎至若周行已之教授本州發明中庸之
旨使人知有伊洛之學又非温州之巨擘
歟雖然浙之風俗善矣而習氣未除人□
盛矣而道學未著我□□□□□氣□□
punctuated:
而其人易治，衣冠文物甲於東南者，寧波也。其人樸靜，而其俗儉約，閭閻之中興行禮遜者，台州也。至於爭訟少而紡績勤，器用備而秔稻足，又非温州之所習尚者乎？以言人物，陸知命之侃然正色，百僚敬憚，王縉之啓沃君心，知無不言，則出於嚴杭者也。陸贄之論諫切直，一本仁義，倪思之論疏剴切，悚動人主，則生於嘉湖者也。金之與衢，則有宗澤之起兵勤王，志在興復，□□之為政簡靜，卒謚清獻者焉。處之與紹，則有葉夢得之博學能文，尤邃經術，嚴光之少有高名，不屈仕進者焉。他如陳禾之引落帝衣，不惜碎首，非寧波所産乎？謝申甫之愛惜名器，扶持正學，非台州所産乎？至若周行已之教授本州，發明中庸之旨，使人知有伊洛之學，又非温州之巨擘歟？

雖然，浙之風俗善矣，而習氣未除；人□盛矣，而道學未著。我□□□□□氣□□
translation_en:
…and its people are easy to govern; Ningbo surpasses the southeast in its cultivated elite and cultural accomplishments. Taizhou’s people are simple and quiet, its customs frugal and restrained, and ritual propriety and deference flourish in its neighborhoods. As for having few lawsuits, working diligently at spinning, possessing ample utensils and supplies, and enjoying an abundance of rice—are these not also the practices esteemed in Wenzhou?

Speaking of eminent figures, Lu Zhiming, upright and solemn in bearing, commanded the respect and awe of the officials; Wang Jin enlightened and nurtured his sovereign’s mind, withholding nothing that he knew. These men came from Yanzhou and Hangzhou. Lu Zhi’s arguments and remonstrances were earnest and forthright, grounded entirely in benevolence and righteousness; Ni Si’s memorials were incisive and deeply stirred his sovereign. These men were born in Jiaxing and Huzhou. Jinhua and Quzhou produced Zong Ze, who raised troops in service of the throne, intent on restoring the dynasty, and [name illegible], whose administration was uncomplicated and tranquil and who received the posthumous name Qingxian. Chuzhou and Shaoxing produced Ye Mengde, broadly learned and accomplished in writing, with particularly profound knowledge of the Classics, and Yan Guang, renowned from his youth, who would not compromise himself to enter official service. As for Chen He, who tugged at the emperor’s robe until it came off [?], undeterred even by the prospect of having his head smashed—was he not a native of Ningbo? Xie Shenfu, who cherished the dignity of official titles and insignia and upheld orthodox learning—was he not a native of Taizhou? And Zhou Xingyi, who taught in his native prefecture, elucidated the meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean, and made people aware of the learning of the Yi and Luo rivers—was he not an outstanding figure of Wenzhou?

Nevertheless, although Zhejiang’s customs are good, ingrained habits have not been eradicated; although its eminent people [?] flourish, the Learning of the Way has not become manifest. Our [illegible passage containing 氣, “vital force” or “ethos”; sense uncertain] …

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
朝
列聖繼作漸摩之以仁義薫陶之以禮樂百有
餘年士生其間當尊德性以立其體道問
學以致其用一以躬行爲先而變其舊染
之習使俗純禮義咸有鄒魯之風人歸道
德悉蹈孔孟之行則庶乎其至也斯志也
非曰能之願學焉執事其進而教之幸甚
第二問
孫鑰
===
同考試官訓導張批答者多得失相半此篇事實
詳明宜表出之
同考試官訓導陸批能知聖人所以爲學之意其留
心古訓者歟
同考試官教諭李批條答明快允宜高薦
考試官訓導桑批知作聖非難而希聖有本必高識之士
考試官教授林批寓希聖之志於言表豪傑士也
論聖人之於學無自足之心人之於聖人
無不可至之理盖天下之理一𡨋而天下
punctuated:
朝列聖繼作，漸摩之以仁義，薫陶之以禮樂，百有餘年。士生其間，當尊德性以立其體，道問學以致其用，一以躬行爲先，而變其舊染之習，使俗純禮義，咸有鄒魯之風；人歸道德，悉蹈孔孟之行，則庶乎其至也。斯志也，非曰能之，願學焉。執事其進而教之，幸甚！

第二問
孫鑰

同考試官訓導張批：答者多得失相半，此篇事實詳明，宜表出之。
同考試官訓導陸批：能知聖人所以爲學之意，其留心古訓者歟！
同考試官教諭李批：條答明快，允宜高薦。
考試官訓導桑批：知作聖非難，而希聖有本，必高識之士。
考試官教授林批：寓希聖之志於言表，豪傑士也。

論聖人之於學，無自足之心；人之於聖人，無不可至之理。盖天下之理一𡨋，而天下
translation_en:
…the successive sage emperors of the dynasty have arisen, gradually shaping the people through benevolence and righteousness and cultivating them through ritual and music for more than a hundred years. Scholars born in this age should honor their moral nature to establish the foundation and pursue inquiry and learning to bring it into practice. They should consistently put personal practice first and transform their ingrained habits, so that customs become wholly imbued with ritual propriety and righteousness, everywhere sharing the ethos of Zou and Lu, and people return to the Way and virtue, all following the conduct of Confucius and Mencius. Then they might approach perfection. Such is my aspiration: I do not claim to be capable of it, but wish to learn. If you, honored examiners, would encourage and instruct me, I would be most grateful.

Second Policy Question
Sun Yue 孫鑰

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor: Most respondents have merits and faults in equal measure. This essay presents historical facts fully and clearly and deserves to be singled out.

Comment by Associate Examiner Lu, Assistant Instructor: He understands the purpose for which the sages pursued learning. Surely he is one who attends closely to ancient teachings!

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: His responses to the individual points are clear and incisive. He truly deserves a high recommendation.

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之事無窮故雖生知之聖亦未嘗自以為
足而不學學而知之則其成功有不異於
生知者天下豈有不可至之聖哉噫聖人
未易言也執事以是為問愚敢不撫所聞
以對書云思曰睿睿作聖聖者無所不通
之謂也故不思而得不勉而中然其心未
始以為足也帝堯聖矣臣之不才若必試
而後知者方命圯族堯不知而誰知乎其
試之者不自以為然也文王聖矣於道猶
===
望而未之見緝熈敬止文王果未見而誰
見乎其望之者不自以為足也周公聖矣
其有未得者仰而思之夜以繼日幸而得
之坐以待旦周公之心曷嘗以為已得而
不加之意哉孔子述堯舜法文武律天時
襲水土古之所謂聖者至是而極姑以其
小者言之對萍實之問則知楚之必霸對
商羊之問則知齊之大水土缶蔵物則知
羵羊為土之恠鉅骨專車則知防風□□
punctuated: 之事無窮，故雖生知之聖，亦未嘗自以為足而不學。學而知之，則其成功有不異於生知者，天下豈有不可至之聖哉？噫！聖人未易言也。執事以是為問，愚敢不撫所聞以對？書云：「思曰睿，睿作聖。」聖者，無所不通之謂也，故不思而得，不勉而中。然其心未始以為足也。帝堯聖矣，臣之不才，若必試而後知者。方命圯族，堯不知而誰知乎？其試之者，不自以為然也。文王聖矣，於道猶望而未之見。緝熈敬止，文王果未見而誰見乎？其望之者，不自以為足也。周公聖矣，其有未得者，仰而思之，夜以繼日；幸而得之，坐以待旦。周公之心曷嘗以為已得而不加之意哉？孔子述堯舜，法文武，律天時，襲水土，古之所謂聖者至是而極。姑以其小者言之：對萍實之問，則知楚之必霸；對商羊之問，則知齊之大水；土缶蔵物，則知羵羊為土之恠；鉅骨專車，則知防風□□
translation_en:
…the affairs of the world are inexhaustible. Thus even a sage born with knowledge has never considered himself sufficient and ceased to learn. Those who gain knowledge through learning can attain achievements no different from those born with knowledge. How, then, could there be a level of sagehood that people cannot attain? Ah! Sages are not easy to discuss. Since you, sir, have posed this question, how dare I fail to draw upon what I have heard in reply?

The Book of Documents says: “Thought should be penetrating; penetration makes a sage.” A sage is one whose understanding reaches everywhere. Thus he grasps things without deliberation and hits the mark without effort. Yet he has never considered himself sufficient.

Emperor Yao was a sage. Yet he seemed to need to test an incapable minister before recognizing his incapacity. Who, if not Yao, would have known that this man defied commands and harmed his kin? His testing him showed that he did not presume his own judgment to be correct. King Wen was a sage. Yet he looked toward the Way as though he had not seen it. He “continued in luminous virtue and rested in reverence.” If King Wen had truly not seen the Way, who had? His looking toward it showed that he did not consider himself sufficient. The Duke of Zhou was a sage. Whenever there was something he had not grasped, he looked upward and pondered it, continuing through the night after the day. If he succeeded in grasping it, he sat awaiting dawn. When did the Duke of Zhou ever think that he had already grasped something and need give it no further attention?

Confucius transmitted the teachings of Yao and Shun, took Kings Wen and Wu as his models, followed the patterns of Heaven’s seasons, and accorded with the conditions of water and soil. What the ancients called sagehood reached its culmination in him. Let us speak only of its lesser manifestations. In answering a question about the floating fruit, he knew that Chu would surely attain hegemony; in answering a question about the Shangyang bird, he knew that Qi would suffer a great flood. When a creature was concealed in an earthen jar, he knew that the Fenyang was an uncanny creature of the earth; when a gigantic bone filled an entire cart, he knew that Fangfeng □□ [?]…

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
骨焉禹之所戮事之小者無不知則大者
不待論矣物之竒者無不知則常者不待
問矣然而終日不食終夜不寢未嘗自以
為極焉老聃之習於禮則問之萇弘之通
於樂則問之郯子之通於官則問之師襄
之通於琴則學之孔子豈獨於此不能哉
名物有定數術業有專攻問而得之則彼
所知者我知之矣學而得之則彼所能者
我能之矣合眾人之長為一己之長而無
===
遺焉此孔子之所以為聖歟若禘之不知
非不知也蓋不易言耳軍旅之未學非未
學也蓋不足言耳封禪之不通非不通也
蓋不屑言耳於其所不易言與其所不足
言不屑言者觀聖人聖人之所知者又可
測乎今之人聞一事則曰我善足矣格一
物則曰我學至矣而欲求至於聖惡可得
哉若孜孜以求汲汲以學舜人也文王我
師也及其成功亦何生知學知之間哉愚
punctuated: 骨焉，禹之所戮。事之小者無不知，則大者不待論矣；物之竒者無不知，則常者不待問矣。然而終日不食，終夜不寢，未嘗自以為極焉。老聃之習於禮，則問之；萇弘之通於樂，則問之；郯子之通於官，則問之；師襄之通於琴，則學之。孔子豈獨於此不能哉？名物有定數，術業有專攻。問而得之，則彼所知者我知之矣；學而得之，則彼所能者我能之矣。合眾人之長為一己之長，而無遺焉，此孔子之所以為聖歟？若禘之不知，非不知也，蓋不易言耳；軍旅之未學，非未學也，蓋不足言耳；封禪之不通，非不通也，蓋不屑言耳。於其所不易言與其所不足言、不屑言者觀聖人，聖人之所知者又可測乎？今之人聞一事，則曰：「我善足矣。」格一物，則曰：「我學至矣。」而欲求至於聖，惡可得哉？若孜孜以求，汲汲以學，舜，人也；文王，我師也。及其成功，亦何生知、學知之間哉？愚
translation_en:
…bones, belonging to the one whom Yu executed. If there was nothing he did not know about even minor affairs, his knowledge of great affairs needs no discussion. If there was nothing he did not know about unusual things, his knowledge of ordinary things needs no questioning. Yet he went all day without eating and all night without sleeping, never considering himself to have reached the utmost limit. Because Lao Dan was versed in ritual, he questioned him; because Chang Hong understood music, he questioned him; because the Viscount of Tan understood official institutions, he questioned him; and because Music Master Xiang understood the zither, he studied with him. Could Confucius alone have lacked ability in these matters? Names and things have their established particulars, and arts and occupations have their specialized fields of study. Once I gain knowledge through questioning, what others know I too know; once I gain ability through study, what others can do I too can do. He combined the strengths of everyone into his own strengths, leaving nothing out. Was this not how Confucius became a sage?

As for his professed ignorance of the di sacrifice, it was not that he did not know: it was simply not easy to speak of. His statement that he had not studied military affairs did not mean he had not studied them: they were simply not worth speaking of. His lack of familiarity with the feng and shan sacrifices did not mean he lacked understanding: he simply disdained to speak of them. If we consider the sage through what he found difficult to discuss, unworthy of discussion, or beneath discussing, can the extent of his knowledge be fathomed?

People today hear of a single matter and say, “My goodness is sufficient.” They investigate a single thing and say, “My learning has reached its utmost.” Yet they wish to attain sagehood—how could they possibly do so? If instead one seeks diligently and studies earnestly, Shun was a human being, and King Wen is my teacher. Once one has achieved success, what distinction remains between knowing from birth and knowing through study? I, foolish as I am, …

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
不敏不足以語此有志於聖人者執事未
可謂世無其人
第三問
吳雲
同考試官學正鄭批用人一策有考據有斷制非經
統問目者比其強學待問者歟
考試官訓導桑批選舉一事處置有條他日用之
必知所從違矣
考試官教授林批酌古準今指陳切當可取
===
當夫用人之柄者莫貴於明莫貴於公尤
莫貴於勇明則無蔽而賢否不至於混淆
公則無私而是非不至於倒置勇則無怯
而予奪不至於撓沮集是三者然後天下
之才可使無遺而天下之事不難乎理矣
嗚呼此大臣宰相之事唐虞三代之所同
然而漢唐以下之所絕無而僅有者也請
為執事論之明揚俊民固宰相之任而知
人其難亦聖知之憂蓋人藏其心不可測
punctuated:
不敏，不足以語此。有志於聖人者，執事未可謂世無其人。

第三問
吳雲

同考試官學正鄭批：用人一策，有考據，有斷制，非經統問目者比，其強學待問者歟？
考試官訓導桑批：選舉一事，處置有條，他日用之，必知所從違矣。
考試官教授林批：酌古準今，指陳切當，可取。

當夫用人之柄者，莫貴於明，莫貴於公，尤莫貴於勇。明則無蔽，而賢否不至於混淆；公則無私，而是非不至於倒置；勇則無怯，而予奪不至於撓沮。集是三者，然後天下之才可使無遺，而天下之事不難乎理矣。嗚呼！此大臣宰相之事，唐虞三代之所同然，而漢唐以下之所絕無而僅有者也。請為執事論之。明揚俊民，固宰相之任，而知人其難，亦聖知之憂。蓋人藏其心，不可測
translation_en:
…I am not clever enough to speak adequately of this. Yet you, sir, cannot say that the world contains no one resolved to emulate the sages.

Third Question
Wu Yun

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, School Instructor: This policy essay on employing men offers supporting evidence and decisive judgments. It is not comparable to essays that merely run through the questions [?]. Is its author not one who studies diligently in readiness to be questioned?

Comment by Examiner Sang, Assistant Instructor: On the matter of selecting and recommending men, his proposed arrangements are orderly. If entrusted with this work in the future, he will surely know what to follow and what to reject.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: He weighs ancient practice against present circumstances; his exposition is pertinent and sound, and merits acceptance.

For those who wield the authority to employ men, nothing is more precious than discernment, nothing more precious than impartiality, and, above all, nothing more precious than courage. Discernment prevents obscured judgment, so that the worthy and unworthy are not confused. Impartiality prevents selfishness, so that right and wrong are not reversed. Courage prevents timidity, so that granting and withdrawing appointments are not thwarted or obstructed. Only when these three qualities are combined can all the talent under Heaven be put to use without omission, and the affairs of the realm be ordered without difficulty. Alas! This is the business of great ministers and chief councilors. It was the common practice under Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties, but from the Han and Tang onward it has been virtually absent, appearing only rarely. Allow me to discuss it for you, sir.

Clearly identifying and promoting outstanding men is indeed the responsibility of chief councilors. Yet the difficulty of knowing men troubled even those possessed of sagely wisdom. For people conceal their hearts, which cannot be fathomed…

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
識直者近訐而剛者近傲佞者似忠而詐
者似信鳳鳴者或鷙其翰羊質者或虎其
皮自非知言窮理如聖賢固難保其不失
於驪黃之外矣愚嘗思之用人者固不可
無定法亦不可拘定法法以待常人若瓌
竒之士豪傑之材則又當以非常之法遇
之此不易之論也莘野傅巖渭濱之事固
不世見然十室之邑必有忠信百歩之内
必有香草堂堂海宇豈無竒偉特出如西
===
漢之爲卿相者乎顧吾所以求之用之者
如何爾大抵非明則有之而不知非公則
知之而不用非勇則用之而不果魏晉隋
唐之間風聲氣習愈趨愈下李粛山濤之
爲吏部甄竒録異品藻曲當是不任資格
也至崔亮裴光庭則不問愚良專較年資
矣夫爲國用人而惟年資是視則闒茸卑
汚者立登要津何怪於當世之譏牛弘之
爲尚書舉先德行而後文才是未崇法律
punctuated: 識。直者近訐，而剛者近傲；佞者似忠，而詐者似信。鳳鳴者或鷙其翰，羊質者或虎其皮。自非知言窮理如聖賢，固難保其不失於驪黃之外矣。愚嘗思之：用人者固不可無定法，亦不可拘定法。法以待常人，若瓌竒之士、豪傑之材，則又當以非常之法遇之，此不易之論也。莘野、傅巖、渭濱之事，固不世見；然十室之邑，必有忠信；百歩之内，必有香草。堂堂海宇，豈無竒偉特出如西漢之爲卿相者乎？顧吾所以求之用之者如何爾。大抵非明，則有之而不知；非公，則知之而不用；非勇，則用之而不果。魏晉隋唐之間，風聲氣習愈趨愈下。李粛、山濤之爲吏部，甄竒録異，品藻曲當，是不任資格也。至崔亮、裴光庭，則不問愚良，專較年資矣。夫爲國用人，而惟年資是視，則闒茸卑汚者立登要津，何怪於當世之譏？牛弘之爲尚書，舉先德行而後文才，是未崇法律
translation_en: … discern. The forthright verge on faultfinding, and the resolute on arrogance; the flattering resemble the loyal, and the deceitful resemble the trustworthy. Some who sing like phoenixes may have the wings of birds of prey; some with the substance of sheep may wear the skins of tigers. Unless one understands words and thoroughly investigates principles as the sages and worthies did, one can hardly be certain of avoiding errors in discerning what lies beyond outward appearances, like a horse’s black or yellow coat. I have often reflected on this: those who employ men certainly cannot dispense with established rules, yet neither can they be bound by them. Rules serve for dealing with ordinary men; extraordinary scholars and men of outstanding ability should be treated by extraordinary means. This is an unalterable principle. The events of the fields of Shen, the cliffs of Fu, and the banks of the Wei River are indeed seldom seen in successive ages. Yet even a settlement of ten households must contain someone loyal and trustworthy, and within a hundred paces there must be fragrant plants. Could this vast and splendid realm lack extraordinary, outstanding men like those who served as chief ministers and grand councilors under the Western Han? It depends only on how we seek them out and employ them. In general, without discernment, such men may exist but go unrecognized; without impartiality, they may be recognized but remain unemployed; without courage, they may be employed without firmness of purpose. During the Wei, Jin, Sui, and Tang, prevailing attitudes and habits declined ever further. When Li Su and Shan Tao served in the Ministry of Personnel, they selected exceptional men and recruited unusual talent, assessing each with meticulous aptness: this meant that they did not rely on formal qualifications and seniority. With Cui Liang and Pei Guangting, however, no inquiry was made into whether men were foolish or worthy; only their years of service were compared. If, in employing men for the state, one looks solely to seniority, then the worthless, base, and corrupt immediately ascend to influential posts. Why be surprised at the criticism of their contemporaries? When Niu Hong served as minister, he gave priority in his recommendations to moral conduct and placed literary talent second; this meant that he had not exalted expertise in laws and statutes …

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
也至戴胄則好抑文雅推獎法吏矣夫求
賢輔治而惟法吏是崇則不學無術者固
居優選奚免於君子之譏常衮為相而賢
愚同滯天下譏之雖盡公守法其何補崔
祐甫繼相而除用得人建中稱治雖舉多
親故其奚害數子之得失固不待較當用
人之柄者於此焉觀之則知所從違矣噫
玉石之分鸞隼之判惟明者乃能辨之若
夫利義之相勝毀譽榮辱之相尋非公且
===
勇而欲成功於當時垂譽於後世亦難矣
愚見如此執事倘有取焉亦士類之幸
第四問
毛實
同考試官訓導李 批歷舉漢唐諸將用兵制勝之策
條答無遺末復以伊吕為法盖欲百尺竿頭進歩者也
考試官訓導桑 批折衷古名將用兵之法皆中肯綮
盖嘗入孫武之室而躊躇四顧者也
考試官教授林 批機軸出於胷中華采流於筆下
punctuated:
也。至戴胄，則好抑文雅，推獎法吏矣。夫求賢輔治，而惟法吏是崇，則不學無術者固居優選，奚免於君子之譏？常衮為相，而賢愚同滯，天下譏之，雖盡公守法，其何補？崔祐甫繼相，而除用得人，建中稱治，雖舉多親故，其奚害？數子之得失，固不待較。當用人之柄者，於此焉觀之，則知所從違矣。噫！玉石之分，鸞隼之判，惟明者乃能辨之。若夫利義之相勝，毀譽榮辱之相尋，非公且勇，而欲成功於當時，垂譽於後世，亦難矣。愚見如此，執事倘有取焉，亦士類之幸。

第四問
毛實

同考試官訓導李批：歷舉漢唐諸將用兵制勝之策，條答無遺。末復以伊吕為法，盖欲百尺竿頭進歩者也。

考試官訓導桑批：折衷古名將用兵之法，皆中肯綮。盖嘗入孫武之室，而躊躇四顧者也。

考試官教授林批：機軸出於胷中，華采流於筆下。
translation_en:
… indeed. Dai Zhou, however, was fond of disparaging literary refinement and promoting officials versed in law. If, in seeking worthy men to assist in government, one honors only legal officials, then men without learning or competence securely occupy the preferred places. How can one escape the criticism of gentlemen? When Chang Gun served as chief minister, the worthy and the foolish alike languished without advancement, and all under Heaven criticized him. Even if he was wholly impartial and observed the rules, what good did that do? Cui Youfu succeeded him as chief minister and appointed suitable men, so that the Jianzhong reign was praised for good government. Even if many of those he recommended were relatives and old acquaintances, what harm did that do? The successes and failures of these men surely need no further comparison. Those who wield the power of appointment need only consider these examples to know what to follow and what to reject. Alas! Only the discerning can distinguish jade from common stone, or a phoenix from a falcon. As for the struggle between personal advantage and righteousness, and the succession of slander and praise, honor and disgrace: without both impartiality and courage, it is difficult indeed to achieve success in one’s own time and leave a good name to posterity. Such is my humble view. If you, sir, find anything worth adopting in it, that too would be a blessing for the community of scholars.

Fourth Question
Mao Shi

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: He cites in succession the strategies by which generals of the Han and Tang deployed their forces and secured victory, answering point by point without omission. At the end he further takes Yi Yin and Lü Shang as models. Evidently he aspires to advance another step from the top of a hundred-foot pole.

Comment by Examiner Sang, Instructor: He weighs and reconciles the methods of warfare employed by famous generals of antiquity, and every point strikes home. Evidently he has entered the inner chamber of Sun Wu’s learning and surveyed his surroundings with assurance.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Professor: Ingenious conceptions arise from his mind, and literary brilliance flows from his brush …

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
使見諸行事必有可觀者矣
甞謂用兵有一定之法用法無一定之機
用兵而無其法是謂徒兵用法而無其機
是謂徒法善用兵者固不可無法而亦豈
可泥於法哉請因明問所及而條陳之夫
兵者國之大事聖人不得已而用之也故
箕子於洪範陳三八政而以師居其末焉
稽之商周伊尹鳴條之役呂望牧野之師
秉鉞之時皆如挟纊麾戈之際咸沁春風
===
不可尚已戰國以還善言兵者莫如孫武
觀其論將之五徳必曰智信仁勇嚴而後
及之於用法蓋能識古者用兵之遺意而
兼以當時制勝之巧術此其法所以後世
用之而不能違也且以漢唐以來諸將之
成功而合於其法者言之若陳湯矯制誅
莎車而成安邉之功是有得於將能而君
不御之法也杜預不施節度於王濬而成
平吳之績非有得於上下同欲□□□□
punctuated:
使見諸行事，必有可觀者矣。

甞謂用兵有一定之法，用法無一定之機。用兵而無其法，是謂徒兵；用法而無其機，是謂徒法。善用兵者，固不可無法，而亦豈可泥於法哉？請因明問所及而條陳之。夫兵者，國之大事，聖人不得已而用之也。故箕子於《洪範》陳三八政，而以師居其末焉。稽之商周，伊尹鳴條之役、呂望牧野之師，秉鉞之時，皆如挟纊；麾戈之際，咸沁春風。不可尚已。戰國以還，善言兵者莫如孫武。觀其論將之五徳，必曰智、信、仁、勇、嚴，而後及之於用法。蓋能識古者用兵之遺意，而兼以當時制勝之巧術，此其法所以後世用之而不能違也。且以漢唐以來諸將之成功而合於其法者言之：若陳湯矯制誅莎車，而成安邉之功，是有得於將能而君不御之法也。杜預不施節度於王濬，而成平吳之績，非有得於上下同欲□□□□
translation_en:
…If these ideas were put into practice, there would surely be something worthy of admiration.

I have long maintained that warfare has fixed principles, but the opportunities for applying them are not fixed. To wage war without its principles is merely to employ troops; to apply principles without grasping the opportune moment is merely to follow rules. Those skilled in warfare certainly cannot dispense with principles, but how could they cling rigidly to them? Allow me to set out my responses in order, following the matters raised in your discerning question.

Warfare is a great affair of state; the sages resorted to it only when they had no alternative. Thus, in the Great Plan, Jizi set forth the third category, the eight affairs of government, placing military affairs last among them. Looking back to the Shang and Zhou, consider Yi Yin’s campaign at Mingtiao and Lü Wang’s army at Muye. When they wielded the battle-axe, all felt as though clothed in silk floss; when they brandished their spears, all were bathed in a spring breeze. Nothing could surpass this.

From the Warring States onward, none discoursed on warfare more skillfully than Sun Wu. Consider his discussion of the five virtues of a commander: he invariably names wisdom, trustworthiness, benevolence, courage, and strictness before proceeding to the application of military principles. He understood the surviving spirit of ancient warfare and combined it with the ingenious techniques for securing victory in his own time. This is why later generations could employ his principles but could not depart from them.

Let us speak, moreover, of successful commanders from the Han and Tang onward whose achievements accorded with his principles. Chen Tang, for example, falsely invoked an imperial decree to punish Shache [?], thereby securing the frontier. This showed his grasp of the principle that the commander must be capable and the ruler must not constrain him. Du Yu refrained from imposing operational directives on Wang Jun and thus achieved the pacification of Wu. Was this not through grasping the principle that superiors and subordinates should share the same aims [four illegible characters]…

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
孝寛以金帛啗齊人而知其動靜是有得
於因間用鄉人之法也于謹因蕭詧有隙
於梁而聽其來附非有得於內間用官人
之法乎韓信遣辯士而舉全燕吳漢收守
長而降五姓所謂不戰而屈人之兵與屈
人之兵而非戰二子有焉班超收穀堅守
而敗月氏之師周訪從杜曾破其兩甄而
有漢沔之捷所謂以飽待飢以佚待勞者
二子有焉屬於廊廟之上以謀其事張良
===
之運籌決勝然也彼充國之征羌而曰兵
難遥度雖不同於良然與其因敵變化以
取勝之說則同兵之情主速馮奉世之一
舉破羌然也彼郭子儀之討懷恩而欲堅
壁以緩賊雖有異於奉世然與其强則避
之之意則合若夫狄青不誅蘇建棄軍之
罪以其以少而敵衆也非知夫小敵之堅
大敵之擒者乎李廣不擊刁斗而得士卒
之心以其用法之簡也非所謂其令素行
punctuated: 孝寛以金帛啗齊人而知其動靜，是有得於因間用鄉人之法也。于謹因蕭詧有隙於梁而聽其來附，非有得於內間用官人之法乎？韓信遣辯士而舉全燕，吳漢收守長而降五姓，所謂不戰而屈人之兵與屈人之兵而非戰，二子有焉。班超收穀堅守而敗月氏之師，周訪從杜曾，破其兩甄而有漢沔之捷，所謂以飽待飢、以佚待勞者，二子有焉。屬於廊廟之上以謀其事，張良之運籌決勝然也。彼充國之征羌而曰「兵難遥度」，雖不同於良，然與其因敵變化以取勝之說則同。兵之情主速，馮奉世之一舉破羌然也。彼郭子儀之討懷恩而欲堅壁以緩賊，雖有異於奉世，然與其强則避之之意則合。若夫狄青不誅蘇建棄軍之罪，以其以少而敵衆也，非知夫小敵之堅、大敵之擒者乎？李廣不擊刁斗而得士卒之心，以其用法之簡也，非所謂其令素行
translation_en:
…Xiaokuan used gold and silk to entice men of Qi and thereby learned their movements: he had grasped the method of employing local inhabitants as local spies. Yu Jin, taking advantage of Xiao Cha’s estrangement from Liang, accepted his submission. Had he not grasped the method of employing officials as inside spies? Han Xin dispatched a persuasive envoy and secured all of Yan; Wu Han won over local administrators and brought the five clans into submission. Both exemplified what is meant by “subduing another’s army without fighting” and “subduing another’s army, but not through battle.” Ban Chao gathered grain and held firm, defeating the army of the Yuezhi; Zhou Fang pursued Du Zeng [?], broke both wings of his army, and won victory in the Han–Mian region. Both exemplified what is meant by “meeting the hungry with well-fed troops, and the weary with rested troops.”

Entrusting the planning of military affairs to those at court is exemplified by Zhang Liang’s devising strategies and determining victory. When Zhao Chongguo campaigned against the Qiang, he said, “Military affairs are difficult to assess from afar.” Though his approach differed from Zhang Liang’s, it accorded with the teaching that victory is won by adapting to changes in the enemy. Speed is essential in warfare: Feng Fengshi’s defeat of the Qiang in a single stroke exemplifies this. When Guo Ziyi campaigned against Huai’en, he sought to hold firm behind fortified walls and wear down the rebels through delay. Though this differed from Feng Fengshi’s approach, it accorded with the principle, “When the enemy is strong, avoid him.”

As for Di Qing [?; the episode concerns Wei Qing], he did not execute Su Jian for the crime of abandoning his army, because Su had faced a numerous enemy with few troops. Did he not understand that “a small force that stubbornly stands its ground becomes the captive of a larger enemy”? Li Guang did not sound the night-watch cauldrons, yet won his soldiers’ hearts through the simplicity of his military regulations. Was this not what is meant by “his orders have consistently been carried out …”

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
與衆相得者乎是皆能用其法而乘之以
機此其所以成功也其果與法背馳邪方
今
列聖統治百有餘年太平之治曠古所無固無
事於兵矣設或邊風搖草塞鼠穿墉職閫
外之寄者必師伊呂以為之本法孫吳以
濟其用庶幾降龍虎之陣於九天張鵝鸛
之軍於萬里使天下後世曉然知仁義之
無敵斯其至矣捧尺一之
===
詔操丈二之殳掃黃磧之飛塵弄私渠之清沘
愚竊有志焉惟執事恕其狂妄而進教幸
甚
第五問
翁健之
同考試官訓導王批時務一策處置得宜其才之有用
者乎是用錄出
同考試官訓導梁批初二場連閱子卷如獲璆琳及觀
時務一策益知為閩海真産實
punctuated:
與衆相得者乎？是皆能用其法而乘之以機，此其所以成功也。其果與法背馳邪？方今列聖統治百有餘年，太平之治，曠古所無，固無事於兵矣。設或邊風搖草，塞鼠穿墉，職閫外之寄者，必師伊呂以為之本，法孫吳以濟其用，庶幾降龍虎之陣於九天，張鵝鸛之軍於萬里，使天下後世曉然知仁義之無敵，斯其至矣。捧尺一之詔，操丈二之殳，掃黃磧之飛塵，弄私渠之清沘，愚竊有志焉。惟執事恕其狂妄而進教，幸甚。
第五問
翁健之
同考試官訓導王批：時務一策，處置得宜，其才之有用者乎？是用錄出。
同考試官訓導梁批：初二場連閱子卷，如獲璆琳。及觀時務一策，益知為閩海真産，實
translation_en:
…and being in harmony with the troops? These men all knew how to employ the methods and apply them as circumstances offered opportunities; this was how they achieved success. Did they really run counter to those methods? Today, our successive sage emperors have ruled for more than a hundred years. Their peaceful government is without precedent in antiquity, and there is assuredly no occasion for warfare. Yet should frontier winds stir the grass and border rats burrow through the walls, those entrusted with military command beyond the gates must take Yi Yin and Lü Shang as their teachers to establish their foundation, and follow Sun Wu and Wu Qi to make their methods effective in practice. They might then bring dragon-and-tiger formations down from the ninth heaven and deploy goose-and-stork armies over ten thousand li, making all under Heaven and later generations clearly understand that benevolence and righteousness are invincible. This would be the highest achievement. To hold aloft an imperial edict on a tablet one chi and one cun long, wield a staff twelve chi long, sweep away the flying dust of the yellow desert, and play in the clear waters of Siqu [?]—I humbly cherish this ambition. I would be most fortunate if you, sir, would forgive my rash presumption and grant me instruction.
Fifth Question
Weng Jianzhi
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor: “In this policy essay on current affairs, his proposed measures are appropriate. Surely his is a talent that can be put to use? For this reason, the essay has been selected for inclusion.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Liang, Assistant Instructor: “Reading your papers in succession in the first and second sessions was like finding precious jade. Upon reading your policy essay on current affairs, I became still more certain that you are a genuine product of the Fujian coast, truly …”

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
天府必爲清廟之用無疑矣
考試官訓導桑批舉全浙之弊而拯濟有方非素
置方楯於胸中其能然邪
考試官教授林批區處事宜迥出人表有識之士也
夫君子居其鄉則知其鄉之俗觀于國則
知其國之政有所見則識之有所憂則懷
之有所謀則思所以行之行之於國而未
能者則思行之於鄉行之於鄉而未能者
有問焉則答之有詢焉則陳之可也愚也
===
賤不敢與聞於國之政請以一鄉之利害
爲執事陳之諸湖之水浙之巨浸藩會之
所仰溉焉者也今淵渚之區半堙爲陸脩
復之令蓋屢議矣而卒尼於豪右之侵占
其弊未可以遽革也今若集其耆民諭以
禍福使知夫侵地之利甚微而溉田之利
甚溥歸地者稍寬他役以酬其勤遏令者
必示重罰而不爲其所撓則水利復而民
亦奚怨之有哉諸場之鹽浙之大利天下
punctuated:
天府，必爲清廟之用，無疑矣。
考試官訓導桑批：舉全浙之弊，而拯濟有方，非素置方楯於胸中，其能然邪？
考試官教授林批：區處事宜，迥出人表，有識之士也。
夫君子居其鄉，則知其鄉之俗；觀于國，則知其國之政。有所見則識之，有所憂則懷之，有所謀則思所以行之。行之於國而未能者，則思行之於鄉；行之於鄉而未能者，有問焉則答之，有詢焉則陳之，可也。愚也賤，不敢與聞於國之政，請以一鄉之利害爲執事陳之。
諸湖之水，浙之巨浸，藩會之所仰溉焉者也。今淵渚之區，半堙爲陸，脩復之令蓋屢議矣，而卒尼於豪右之侵占，其弊未可以遽革也。今若集其耆民，諭以禍福，使知夫侵地之利甚微，而溉田之利甚溥；歸地者稍寬他役，以酬其勤；遏令者必示重罰，而不爲其所撓，則水利復，而民亦奚怨之有哉？諸場之鹽，浙之大利，天下
translation_en:
…the imperial treasury; it will assuredly be put to use in the august ancestral temple.
Examiner Sang, an Instructor, comments: He sets forth the abuses throughout Zhejiang and offers sound means of remedying them. Could he have done this without long having held plans and shields [?] within his breast?
Examiner Lin, a Professor, comments: His handling of practical affairs far surpasses that of others. He is a man of discernment.
When a gentleman lives in his native locality, he learns its customs; when he observes the realm, he learns its government. What he sees, he remembers; what concerns him, he keeps at heart; what he plans, he considers how to carry out. What he cannot carry out in the realm, he considers carrying out in his locality. What he cannot carry out in his locality, he may explain when questioned and set forth when consulted. I am ignorant and of lowly station, and dare not presume to participate in deliberations on the government of the realm. Allow me to set before you, Sir, the benefits and harms affecting a single locality.
The waters of the various lakes constitute Zhejiang’s great bodies of water, upon which the provincial capital depends for irrigation. Today, half these deep pools and shallows have been filled in and turned into dry land. Orders for their restoration have repeatedly been discussed, but in the end have been obstructed by the encroachments of powerful local families. These abuses cannot be immediately eliminated. If the local elders were now assembled and instructed in the harmful and beneficial consequences, they could be made to understand that the gains from encroaching upon this land are very small, whereas the benefits of irrigating the fields are very extensive. Those who return the land should receive some reduction in their other labor obligations to reward their efforts. Those who obstruct the orders must be subjected to severe punishment, without allowing them to thwart the undertaking. Then the irrigation works would be restored, and what cause would the people have for resentment? The salt from the various salterns is a great source of wealth for Zhejiang, and all under Heaven…

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之所仰給焉者也今課額之數半粍為虛
清理之法盖累行矣而竟格於勢家之橫
奪其弊未可以輕去也若覈實以稽之執
法以平之附勢者無所恣其情私鬻者不
得以肆其欲則商賈足而國亦何不足之
患哉銀冶之利其始甚厚也今以私銀代
公課課日粍而民之爭闘者亦益繁豈非
並緣掊克之弊交病之邪故必使出納有
制而司籍簿者不乘之為鼠竊之姦撫字
===
有素而領承宣者不假是為狼貪之計則
官課充於上私闘息於下而上下皆安矣
海道之備其初甚嚴也今以惰兵充重衛
衛日怠而民之從盜者亦益眾豈非教養
禁制之法有未盡邪故必使民有恒產而
仰事俯育之費無俟於他求兵有常律而
坐作進退之法不怠於無教則民業安於
內夷寇靖於外而內外咸寧矣究四者之
害皆久而後成圖四者之利必漸而後復
punctuated:
之所仰給焉者也。今課額之數，半粍為虛。清理之法，盖累行矣，而竟格於勢家之橫奪，其弊未可以輕去也。若覈實以稽之，執法以平之，附勢者無所恣其情，私鬻者不得以肆其欲，則商賈足，而國亦何不足之患哉？銀冶之利，其始甚厚也。今以私銀代公課，課日粍，而民之爭闘者亦益繁，豈非並緣掊克之弊交病之邪？故必使出納有制，而司籍簿者不乘之為鼠竊之姦；撫字有素，而領承宣者不假是為狼貪之計。則官課充於上，私闘息於下，而上下皆安矣。
海道之備，其初甚嚴也。今以惰兵充重衛，衛日怠，而民之從盜者亦益眾，豈非教養禁制之法有未盡邪？故必使民有恒產，而仰事俯育之費無俟於他求；兵有常律，而坐作進退之法不怠於無教。則民業安於內，夷寇靖於外，而內外咸寧矣。究四者之害，皆久而後成；圖四者之利，必漸而後復。
translation_en:
…on which the realm relies for its supply. Now half the assessed tax quota has been dissipated, leaving an empty figure. Measures to set matters in order have repeatedly been implemented, yet have ultimately been obstructed by the forcible appropriation of powerful families. These abuses cannot easily be eliminated. If actual quantities are verified through audits and fairness secured through enforcement of the law, those who attach themselves to the powerful will have no scope to indulge their whims, and illicit sellers will be unable to give free rein to their desires. Merchants will then have enough, and what need will the state have to fear insufficiency? The profits from silver mining and smelting were initially very substantial. Now privately obtained silver is substituted for the public tax obligation; tax receipts dwindle daily, while disputes and fighting among the people grow ever more frequent. Is this not because the abuses of exploiting connections [?] and oppressive exaction afflict them together? Receipts and disbursements must therefore be regulated, so that those in charge of registers and accounts cannot exploit them for furtive theft like rats. Care for the people must be consistently practiced, so that those entrusted with transmitting and carrying out imperial commands cannot use their position for schemes of wolfish rapacity. Then official tax revenues will be sufficient above, private fighting will cease below, and those above and below will all be at peace.
Coastal defenses were initially very strict. Now indolent soldiers fill important garrison posts; defense grows more lax each day, while ever more people join the pirates. Is this not because measures for instruction, sustenance, prohibition, and control have not been fully implemented? The people must therefore have secure livelihoods, so that they need not seek other means to meet the costs of supporting their parents and raising their children. Soldiers must have standing regulations, so that the prescribed movements of sitting, rising, advancing, and retreating do not become lax through lack of training. Then the people's occupations will be secure within, foreign raiders will be quelled without, and peace will prevail both within and without. On examining the harm in these four matters, one finds that it developed only over a long period; in planning to restore their benefits, recovery must likewise come gradually.

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
此居是邦者所不敢知而亦當仁者之所
不敢讓也執事其采而聞諸
廟堂之上則芻蕘之獻亦豈必無涓埃之益
也哉
punctuated: 此居是邦者所不敢知，而亦當仁者之所不敢讓也。執事其采而聞諸廟堂之上，則芻蕘之獻亦豈必無涓埃之益也哉！
translation_en: …These are matters on which one dwelling in this province dares not presume to pronounce, yet neither does one who recognizes a duty of benevolence dare to shirk them. If you, Sir, would take up these suggestions and bring them to the attention of the imperial court, might not this humble offering from a gatherer of grass and firewood yield some benefit, however slight?

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試録後序
人才養之久則盛盛而旋取
用之則不至失旦而無成
國家陶育士類百有餘年每三
載一開科挍其尤公卿百執
事之選咸出是途號爲得人
成化丙午浙江當大比之秋
===
鎖院日巡按監察御史荆茂
洎藩臬提調監試與悅等凡
有事於試事者咸矢心誓神
期得眞才以應世用時士之
抱藝来試者霧滃雲集發而
爲文皆能脫去凡近出入仁
義而非苟作者精加披選共
punctuated:
浙江鄉試録後序

人才養之久則盛，盛而旋取用之，則不至失旦而無成。國家陶育士類百有餘年，每三載一開科，挍其尤，公卿百執事之選咸出是途，號爲得人。

成化丙午，浙江當大比之秋，鎖院日，巡按監察御史荆茂洎藩臬提調監試與悅等，凡有事於試事者，咸矢心誓神，期得眞才以應世用。時士之抱藝来試者霧滃雲集，發而爲文，皆能脫去凡近，出入仁義，而非苟作者。精加披選，共
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

When talented men are nurtured over a long period, they flourish. If, once they flourish, they are promptly selected for service, they will not miss their moment [?] and accomplish nothing. The dynasty has cultivated scholars for more than a hundred years. Every three years it holds an examination to assess the most outstanding among them. Those selected as dukes, ministers, and the many other officials all come through this route, which is renowned for securing worthy men.

In the bingwu year of the Chenghua reign [1486], autumn brought Zhejiang’s triennial examination. On the day the examination compound was sealed, Jing Mao, the Regional Inspecting Censor, together with the proctors and examination overseers from the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions, myself, Yue, and all others engaged in the examination, pledged our hearts and swore before the spirits, intent on obtaining men of genuine talent to meet the needs of the age. At that time, scholars bringing their literary accomplishments to the examination gathered like billowing mist and clouds. When they expressed themselves in writing, all could rise above the commonplace and superficial, ranging through benevolence and righteousness; theirs were no careless compositions. We scrutinized and selected their work with particular care, obtaining in all …

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
得九十人遵定額也悅濫司
去取之衡錄成因序於後日
國家設科取士非特榮諸士也
士之發身科目非欲自榮也
皆所以爲天下而已矣治天
下亘古今惟二道經與變是
也學純於王謂之經經一而
===
變殊乘之而駿發謂之機貼
之而沛蒸謂之時激之而坂
下謂之勢是數者皆變也經
者變之神變者經之郛闔而
闢之弛而張之操之縱之運
用之莫測其兆而曰機曰時
曰勢雖枝葉迷漫而莫不根
punctuated: 得九十人，遵定額也。悅濫司去取之衡，錄成，因序於後日：「國家設科取士，非特榮諸士也；士之發身科目，非欲自榮也。皆所以爲天下而已矣。治天下，亘古今惟二道，經與變是也。學純於王，謂之經。經一而變殊，乘之而駿發謂之機，貼之而沛蒸謂之時，激之而坂下謂之勢。是數者皆變也。經者，變之神；變者，經之郛。闔而闢之，弛而張之，操之縱之，運用之莫測其兆，而曰機、曰時、曰勢。雖枝葉迷漫，而莫不根
translation_en: …ninety men were selected, in accordance with the prescribed quota. I, Yue, unworthily held the balance governing acceptance and rejection. Once the record was completed, I appended these prefatory remarks [?]: “The state establishes examinations to select men for service, not merely to confer honor upon them; men embark upon official careers through the examinations, not to seek honor for themselves. Both are solely for the sake of all under Heaven. In governing all under Heaven, throughout antiquity and the present, there have been only two ways: constancy and adaptation to change. Learning devoted purely to the way of the true king is called constancy. Constancy is one, while changes are manifold. That which one rides to advance swiftly is called opportunity; that to which one adheres to flourish abundantly is called timeliness [?]; that which, once stirred, rushes down a slope is called momentum. These all belong to change. Constancy is the animating spirit of change; change is the outer enclosure of constancy. Closing and opening, relaxing and tightening, holding and releasing—its operations leave no discernible signs of what is to come, yet we speak of opportunity, timeliness, and momentum. Though the branches and leaves spread profusely, none is without roots…

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
本於王霸者特假之而已不
神於王鎔之汞化是以君子
弗學之也今夫海掀之而爲
浪噴之而爲漪鬨之而爲濤
浪也漪也濤也化之皆水也
不觀之海圖乎有浪焉漪焉
濤焉皆假也其可化而爲水
===
否邪皐夔稷契之經濟眞海
也蕭曹房杜之斡旋海圖也
易曰差之毫釐繆以千里此
之謂也悅幼以王道爲學以
爲平生律己誨人之憑藉諸
士子既登名是錄欲上春官
對
punctuated:
本於王。霸者特假之而已，不神於王鎔之汞化，是以君子弗學之也。今夫海，掀之而爲浪，噴之而爲漪，鬨之而爲濤。浪也，漪也，濤也，化之皆水也。不觀之海圖乎？有浪焉，漪焉，濤焉，皆假也。其可化而爲水否邪？皐夔稷契之經濟，眞海也；蕭曹房杜之斡旋，海圖也。《易》曰：「差之毫釐，繆以千里。」此之謂也。
悅幼以王道爲學，以爲平生律己誨人之憑藉。諸士子既登名是錄，欲上春官，對
translation_en:
…are rooted in the kingly way. Hegemons merely borrow from it; they do not attain the wondrous efficacy of the kingly way’s smelting and mercurial transformation [?]. Thus the gentleman does not study their methods. Consider the sea: when heaved up, it becomes waves; when sprayed forth, ripples; when tumultuously stirred, billows. Waves, ripples, and billows, through all their transformations, are water. Have you not observed a picture of the sea? There are waves, ripples, and billows in it, but all are imitations. Can they be transformed into water? The statecraft of Gao, Kui, Ji, and Xie is the real sea; the maneuvering of Xiao, Cao, Fang, and Du is a picture of the sea. The Book of Changes says: “A discrepancy of a hair’s breadth leads to an error of a thousand li.” This is what it means.
From youth, I, Yue, have studied the kingly way, taking it as my lifelong foundation for disciplining myself and instructing others. Now that you candidates have had your names entered in this record, you aspire to present yourselves before the Ministry of Rites and respond…

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
大廷將有致
君之途斯道不於諸士子告而奚
告哉雖然王道不可以易學
予嘗盡心於是而未之有得
者也必主敬以凝之問學以
聚之髙立志以基之廣拓量
以容之能是四者然後本心
===
瑩而萬變通一或失之不渙
則淺不卑則狹矣外有不窮
之變內主不雜之王旣進於
是道矣吾知有股肱耳目之
寄必遡漢唐而上之一以唐
虞三代之事業爲終身事
君之準正猶望燕而北轅雖未至
punctuated: 大廷，將有致君之途，斯道不於諸士子告而奚告哉？雖然，王道不可以易學。予嘗盡心於是，而未之有得者也。必主敬以凝之，問學以聚之，髙立志以基之，廣拓量以容之。能是四者，然後本心瑩而萬變通。一或失之，不渙則淺，不卑則狹矣。外有不窮之變，內主不雜之王。旣進於是道矣，吾知有股肱耳目之寄，必遡漢唐而上之，一以唐虞三代之事業爲終身事君之準。正猶望燕而北轅，雖未至
translation_en: …at the imperial court, they will have a path by which to guide their ruler to perfection. To whom, if not these candidates, should I explain this Way? Yet the Kingly Way cannot be learned lightly. I have devoted my utmost efforts to it, but have not yet attained it. One must maintain reverent attentiveness to consolidate it, inquire and study to accumulate it, set lofty aspirations to establish its foundation, and broaden one’s capacity to accommodate it. Only when one can do these four things will the original mind become luminous and comprehend the myriad transformations. If even one is neglected, one will be either scattered or shallow, either low in aspiration or narrow in capacity. Outside are inexhaustible changes; within, one maintains an unmixed kingly principle [?]. Once they have advanced in this Way, I know that, when entrusted with serving as the ruler’s arms and legs, ears and eyes, they will trace their models back beyond the Han and Tang, taking the achievements of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and the Three Dynasties alone as the standard for serving their ruler throughout their lives. It is just like setting one’s sights on Yan and pointing one’s carriage north: although one has not yet arrived…

title: 成化二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
燕終不至於至越也尚何功
名之足云哉舜何人哉希之
則是諸士子其勗諸他日使
朝廷獲真儒之用而天下蒙至
治之澤則斯科庶有光於萬
世
江西吉安府泰和縣儒學訓
===
導桑悅謹序
punctuated:
燕，終不至於至越也。尚何功名之足云哉！舜何人哉？希之則是。諸士子其勗諸！他日使朝廷獲真儒之用，而天下蒙至治之澤，則斯科庶有光於萬世。
江西吉安府泰和縣儒學訓導桑悅謹序。
translation_en:
…Yan, one will never end up reaching Yue. What need, then, even to speak of achievements and fame! What sort of man was Shun? Aspire to be like him, and you can become such a man. You candidates, exert yourselves! If in days to come the imperial court gains the service of true Confucian scholars, and all under Heaven receive the blessings of perfect governance, then this examination may shine through ten thousand generations.
Preface respectfully composed by Sang Yue, Assistant Instructor in the Confucian School of Taihe County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi.
